definition_zh: 撤走；撤回；退出；取（款）；（从活动中）抽身
definition_en: to pull something back or take it out, and to remove oneself from a place, a plan or an activity
core_image: 一只手伸向桌上的文件，忽然停住，又把它抽回到自己身边
scene: 话才说到一半，他伸手想把文件推回去，手指在纸角上停了一下，又慢慢抽了回来。 She withdrew her application at the last minute.
sceneCN: 这里 withdraw 是「撤回、收回」（第 1 个义项：把已经拿出或提出的东西抽回来）；句意为她在最后一刻撤回了申请。手指在纸角上停一下又抽回来的那一刻，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 撤回；取款；退出
内向的；不愿交往的
退缩的
前进；推进（反义）

senses.title: To take money out
senses.definition: to take money out of a bank account or a machine
senses.definitionCN: 从银行账户或取款机中取出钱
senses.example: He withdrew two hundred yuan to pay the driver.
senses.exampleCN: 他取了二百元付给司机。
senses.why: The verb pulls something from where it was kept, and money in an account is simply a thing kept somewhere.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词把东西从它被存放的地方拉出来，账户里的钱也只是存放在某处的东西。

senses.title: To take back a statement or offer
senses.definition: to say that something you offered or said is no longer in force
senses.definitionCN: 声明自己提出或说过的事不再有效
senses.example: She withdrew her application at the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 她在最后一刻撤回了申请。
senses.why: Once a word or a paper has been handed over, pulling it back means putting it out of play.
senses.whyCN: 一旦话或文件交了出去，把它拉回来就意味着作废。

senses.title: To leave a place or activity
senses.definition: to remove troops or oneself from a place, a contest or an organisation
senses.definitionCN: 把军队或自己从某地、某场比赛或某组织中撤出
senses.example: The team withdrew from the competition after two injuries.
senses.exampleCN: 两人受伤之后，这支队伍退出了比赛。
senses.why: The physical picture of pulling back became a public act of leaving a stage.
senses.whyCN: 往回拉的身体画面，成了退出舞台的公开行为。

senses.title: To pull away into oneself
senses.definition: to become quiet and avoid other people, often because of worry or hurt
senses.definitionCN: 变得沉默、回避他人，常因忧虑或受伤
senses.example: After the quarrel he withdrew into his own room for days.
senses.exampleCN: 争吵之后他躲进自己的房间里好些天。
senses.why: The same motion turned inward describes a person drawing back from company.
senses.whyCN: 同样的动作转向内心，就形容一个人从人群中退回去。

intro.en: Withdraw is a native compound: the old prefix with-, meaning away or back, joined to draw, to pull.
intro.cn: withdraw 是本土复合词：古前缀 with-（离开、往回）加上 draw（拉）。

items.en: wið meant against or away, and dragan meant to draw or pull, so the pair named pulling back.
items.cn: wið 意为对着或离开，dragan 意为拉，两者合起来就是往回拉。

items.en: Early uses described drawing back a hand, an arrow or a knife.
items.cn: 早期用法描述把手、箭或刀抽回来。

items.en: The compound widened to pulling troops back from a place.
items.cn: 复合词扩展到把军队从某地撤回。

items.en: Banking gave the everyday sense of taking money out of an account.
items.cn: 银行业给了它从账户取钱这一日常义项。

items.en: Modern use adds leaving a competition and drawing away from people emotionally.
items.cn: 现代用法又加上了退出比赛与情感上疏远他人。

note.en: The first group collects members of the with- family and look-alikes, the second verbs of taking back or leaving.
note.cn: 第一组收 with- 家族成员与形近词，第二组收表示收回或离开的动词。

entries.definition: The noun of taking back or out.
To refuse to give something due.
To resist and bear pressure.
The past form of the verb.
To move back from an enemy or a difficulty.
Formally to take back a statement.
To put money into an account.

normalIntro.en: Withdraw splits neatly into with and draw, so the picture is simply drawing something back.
normalIntro.cn: withdraw 干净地分成 with 与 draw 两半，画面就是往回拉东西。

normal.en: With plus draw: draw back what you once put out.
normal.cn: with 加 draw：把曾经伸出去的东西拉回来。

normal.en: The past tense is withdrew, with the same vowel change as drew.
normal.cn: 过去式 withdrew，元音变化与 drew 一致。

normal.en: The past participle withdrawn ends like known and shown.
normal.cn: 过去分词 withdrawn 的结尾像 known、shown。

normal.en: Take out money or take back a promise: both are pulling, one from a box and one from a mouth.
normal.cn: 取钱与收回承诺都是拉：一个从箱子里，一个从嘴里。

normal.en: Withhold only holds, so it refuses; withdraw pulls, so it removes.
normal.cn: withhold 只是握住，所以是拒绝给；withdraw 是拉，所以是拿掉。

abstract.en: A hand hesitating over the corner of a paper.
abstract.cn: 一只手在纸角上方犹豫。

abstract.en: A crowd thinning at the edge of the field.
abstract.cn: 场地边缘渐渐稀疏的人群。

abstract.en: A door closing quietly from the inside.
abstract.cn: 一扇从里面轻轻关上的门。

examples.en: The bank charges a fee to withdraw cash abroad.
examples.cn: 在国外取现银行会收手续费。

examples.en: They withdrew the product after a safety warning.
examples.cn: 一则安全警告之后，他们撤下这款产品。

examples.en: Several countries withdrew from the talks.
examples.cn: 有几个国家退出了谈判。

dict_mnemonic.text: with（往回）+ draw（拉）—— 往回拉，就是「撤回、取款」。

root: 古英语 wið（离开、对着）+ dragan（拉）→ withdraw；同族有 withdrawal、withhold、withstand。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as pulling a thing back, then takes money from an account, a promise from circulation, and a person from a stage or from company.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从往回拉开始，接着从账户取钱、让承诺作废，再把人从舞台或人群中撤回。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pulling a document back towards the chest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把文件拉回胸前。

chain: TO TAKE OUT WHAT WAS KEPT
THE PAST PARTICIPLE AS AN ADJECTIVE

branches.en: The money branch: cash taken out for a taxi.
branches.cn: 金钱分支：取出现金付车钱。

branches.en: The promise branch: an application pulled back.
branches.cn: 承诺分支：被撤回的申请。

branches.en: The public branch: a team leaving a competition.
branches.cn: 公共分支：退出比赛的队伍。

branches.en: The private branch: days spent alone in a room.
branches.cn: 私人分支：独自待在房里的几天。

branches.en: The inward branch: the same pull, now aimed at oneself.
branches.cn: 内向分支：同一个拉的动作，如今朝向自己。

intro.en: Withdraw takes the old prefix with- and the root draw, then adds -al to make the noun withdrawal.
intro.cn: withdraw 由古前缀 with- 与词根 draw 组成，再加 -al 得到名词 withdrawal。

latinIntro.en: Both parts are Germanic; the Latin entries below are borrowed cousins for the idea of pulling back.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都属于日耳曼语；下面的拉丁条目只是表示「拉回」的借入表亲。

items.example: It gives the direction of the pulling.

items.exampleCN: 这里前缀是对抗的意思。

items.meaning: the past action of drawing back
in the act of pulling back

definition_zh: 冒险事业；风险投资；动词：敢于去、冒险做；大胆提出
definition_en: a risky or daring enterprise, or to go somewhere or say something despite the danger
core_image: 一条小船离开熟悉的岸边，驶向看不清的雾里
scene: 天还没亮，几条渔船却已经解开缆绳驶向外海。 Few boats ventured out in such heavy fog.
sceneCN: 这里 venture 是「冒险前往」（第 3 个义项：冒着风险去某处）；句意为浓雾之中很少有船敢出海。小船离岸驶入雾里，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：冒险事业；风险投资；投机
动词：冒险前往；敢于做；大胆提出

collocations.zh: 冒昧地做某事；斗胆做某事

derivatives.zh: 由本词加后缀 -some 构成，义为「好冒险的；敢于尝试的」
加后缀 -er 构成，义为「冒险者；合资经营参与者」
同源自拉丁语 advenire 的词，义为「冒险；奇遇」
与 adventure 同源，义为「爱冒险的」

senses.title: A daring enterprise
senses.titleCN: 冒险事业：有风险的事业
senses.definition: a new business activity or project that involves risk of loss
senses.definitionCN: 一项承担亏损风险的新生意或新项目
senses.example: Opening a shop in a quiet town was a bold venture.
senses.exampleCN: 在冷清的小镇开店是一次大胆的冒险事业。
senses.why: Latin venire means to come, and what is ventured is an outcome that has not yet come; you commit before you know it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 venire 意为「来」，venture 的结果尚未到来；你在知道结果之前就已经下了注。

senses.title: Money put at risk
senses.titleCN: 风险投资：押上去的资本
senses.definition: money or capital invested in a risky project in the hope of large profit
senses.definitionCN: 投入有风险项目、期望高额回报的资金
senses.example: The firm put its first venture capital into a small software team.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司把第一笔风险投资投给了一个小型软件团队。
senses.why: The abstract enterprise becomes a sum of money: the risk is now measurable in cash.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的冒险事业化为具体的金额：风险此时可以用钱来衡量。

senses.title: To dare to go
senses.titleCN: 冒险前往：敢去某个地方
senses.definition: to go somewhere that may be dangerous or unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 敢于前往可能危险或令人不快的地方
senses.example: No one ventured into the flooded tunnel.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人冒险进入那条被淹的隧道。
senses.why: The verb keeps the picture of leaving safe ground: the body moves first, the guarantee comes later or never.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了离开安全地面这一画面：身体先动，保障之后才来，也许永远不来。

senses.title: To dare to say
senses.definition: to say or suggest something that may be unwelcome or may be wrong
senses.definitionCN: 敢于说出可能不受欢迎或可能出错的话
senses.example: May I venture a different explanation?
senses.exampleCN: 我可以冒昧地提一个不同的解释吗？
senses.why: Speaking up is also a step into the open; the speaker risks being wrong in front of others.
senses.whyCN: 开口说话同样是走进开阔处；说话人要冒着在众人面前出错的风险。

senses.title: To try something new
senses.titleCN: 敢于尝试：试着做没做过的事
senses.definition: to attempt something new or difficult despite the chance of failure
senses.definitionCN: 尽管可能失败，仍尝试新事物或难做的事
senses.example: She ventured a smile at the stranger across the aisle.
senses.exampleCN: 她朝过道上那位陌生人试着笑了一下。
senses.why: The core image is small here but unchanged: a step taken without knowing how it will be received.
senses.whyCN: 这里的意象虽小却没有改变：在不知道会被如何接受的情况下迈出一步。

intro.en: Venture is a clipped form of adventure, which came from Latin through Old French; the family all turns on the verb 'to come'.
intro.cn: venture 是 adventure 的截短形式，后者经由古法语来自拉丁语；整个词族都围绕「来」这个动词。

items.en: The verb venire meant 'to come'; its future participle venturus described what is going to come.
items.cn: 动词 venire 意为「来」，其将来分词 venturus 指「将要到来的事」。

items.en: Medieval Latin adventura meant 'things about to happen', used for what fate would bring.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 adventura 意为「将要发生的事」，用来指命运会带来什么。

items.en: Old French aventure carried the sense of chance, hazard and a risky undertaking.
items.cn: 古法语 aventure 带有「机遇、风险、冒险之举」的意思。

items.en: English borrowed aventure in the thirteenth century; the shorter venture split off as a separate word.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 aventure；较短的形式 venture 后来独立成一个词。

items.en: Commerce made venture a practical word: joint venture and venture capital name enterprises with money at risk.
items.cn: 商业让 venture 变成务实之词：joint venture 与 venture capital 都指押着钱的经营行为。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same 'come' family; the near-meaning group gathers nouns and verbs for risk-taking.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「来」词根的一族词；近义组收表示冒险的名词与动词。

entries.definition: An exciting or dangerous experience; the longer form from which venture was cut.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「冒险、奇遇」，是 venture 由之截短的较长形式。

entries.definition: Something that happens; literally that which comes out.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事件」，字面意思就是「出来的事」。

entries.definition: To stop something from coming about; pre- plus venire.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「阻止」，由 pre- 加 venire「来」构成。

entries.definition: To devise something new; literally to come upon an idea.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「发明」，字面上是「碰上、遇见」一个想法。

entries.definition: The chance of loss itself; venture is the undertaking that carries it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「风险」，指损失的可能性本身；venture 是承担风险的那件事。

entries.definition: To bet on an uncertain result; more openly about chance and money.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「赌博、押注」，更直接地指机会与金钱。

entries.definition: A task or project one commits to, without the stress on danger.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「承担的事业、任务」，不特别强调危险。

entries.definition: To be bold enough to do something frightening; the nerve rather than the project.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「敢于」，强调胆量而非事业本身。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb venire and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语动词 venire，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: venture is adventure without the ad: the same risky trip, said shorter.
normal.cn: venture 就是去掉 ad 的 adventure：同一趟冒险，说得更短。

normal.en: Joint venture is a business born of two partners, both risking money.
normal.cn: joint venture 是两家合作生出的生意，双方都押了钱。

normal.en: Venture capital names money that dares to fund an unproven idea.
normal.cn: venture capital 指敢去资助尚未验证的想法的钱。

normal.en: To venture out is to leave the house when the weather warns against it.
normal.cn: venture out 就是在天气示警时仍走出家门。

normal.en: Nothing ventured, nothing gained: no risk taken means no gain made.
normal.cn: 不入虎穴焉得虎子：不承担风险就得不到收获。

abstract.en: See the word as a boat leaving the harbour: the shore is the known, the fog is the coming, and the boat moves before it can see.
abstract.cn: 把这个词想成一条离港的小船：岸是已知，雾是将要到来的事，而船在看清之前就已经出发。

abstract.en: Everything in the word happens before the result arrives: venture is always on the side of the untested.
abstract.cn: 这个词说的事都发生在结果到来之前：venture 永远站在未经检验的一边。

abstract.en: The same move can be a business, a journey or a sentence; all three are steps into the open.
abstract.cn: 同一个动作可以是一桩生意、一段路程或一句话；三者都是走进开阔处的一步。

examples.en: They launched a small venture selling solar lamps to remote villages.
examples.cn: 他们创办了一家小型企业，向偏远村庄销售太阳能灯。

examples.en: Nobody ventured outside until the storm had passed.
examples.cn: 暴风雨过去之前，没有人敢出门。

examples.en: The two firms formed a joint venture to build the bridge.
examples.cn: 这两家公司组建合资企业来修建这座桥。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「万一扯」——船万一被扯离岸边，就只能往前闯：冒险

root: 为 adventure 的截短形式，源自拉丁语 venire「来」的将来分词 venturus「将要来临的」，经中世纪拉丁语 adventura 与古法语 aventure 进入英语；同族词有 event、prevent、invent。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of venture run from the abstract enterprise to the capital behind it, then to the small daily daring of going, saying and trying.
sensesIntro.cn: venture 的五个义项从抽象的冒险事业出发，到其背后的资本，再到出门、开口、试探这些日常里的小胆量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boat leaves the shore and steers into fog before it can see the far side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条船离开岸边，在看清对岸之前就驶进雾里。

branches.en: MONEY LINE: the risky project and the capital that funds it.
branches.cn: 资本线：冒险的项目以及资助它的资金。

branches.en: BODY LINE: the feet move into a place that may harm them.
branches.cn: 身体线：双脚走进可能有害的地方。

branches.en: VOICE LINE: the mouth risks a remark that may be wrong.
branches.cn: 声音线：嘴巴冒着出错的风险说出看法。

branches.en: GESTURE LINE: the smallest step, a smile offered to a stranger.
branches.cn: 姿态线：最小的一步，比如向陌生人递出的微笑。

branches.en: CONTRAST: adventure is the same word with more colour, venture the cooler business face.
branches.cn: 对照线：adventure 更带色彩，venture 则是更冷静的商业面孔。

intro.en: Venture inherits a Latin verb stem plus English endings; its parts are transparent once the family is known.
intro.cn: venture 继承了拉丁语动词词干并接英语词尾；认识这个词族之后，各部分都很清楚。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is verifiable: venire, to come, with its participle venturus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础有据可查：venire「来」及其分词 venturus。

items.example: It carries the core of the word.
It turns the verb stem into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词词干变成名词。

definition_zh: 障碍物；阻碍；障碍；绊脚石；壁垒
definition_en: something that stands in the way and must be removed, crossed or gone around before progress can continue
core_image: 一条小径正中横着一块大石，行人提着包从旁边的窄缝侧身挤过
scene: 山道正中倒着一棵大树，骑车的人只好下车，抬着车从路旁的草坡绕过去。 A fallen tree became an obstacle on the mountain road.
sceneCN: 这里指挡在路上的实物（第 1 个义项：物理障碍物）；句意为倒下的树成了山道上的障碍。图中可辨识物件：横倒的树干、单车、草坡、被堵住的路面；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加表示路线的名词构成的复合说法，义为「障碍赛道」；本词没有常见的派生词族
由本词加表示比赛的名词构成的复合说法，义为「障碍赛」
本词的复数形式，义为「多处障碍」

senses.title: A physical thing blocking the way
senses.definition: an object that physically prevents passage along a route
senses.definitionCN: 物理上阻止人沿路线通行的物体
senses.example: A fallen tree became an obstacle on the mountain road.
senses.exampleCN: 倒下的树成了山道上的障碍。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to stand against; the noun first names a thing that literally stands in front of you.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「站在对面」；这个名词最初指一件字面意义上立在你面前的东西。

senses.title: A hindrance to progress
senses.definition: a condition, rule or shortage that slows or prevents an intended outcome
senses.definitionCN: 减缓或阻止预期结果的条件、规则或短缺
senses.example: Lack of funding is the main obstacle to the research.
senses.exampleCN: 资金不足是这项研究的主要障碍。
senses.why: Once the thing standing in the way is no longer physical, the word keeps the same geometry: something is in front of the goal.
senses.whyCN: 当挡路之物不再有形，这个词仍保留同样的几何关系：有东西横在目标前面。

senses.title: A hurdle in sport
senses.titleCN: 体育比赛中的栏架与障碍
senses.definition: a fence, hurdle or water jump that a competitor must clear
senses.definitionCN: 选手必须越过的栏架、栅栏或水沟
senses.example: She cleared every obstacle in the final lap.
senses.exampleCN: 她在最后一圈越过了每一个障碍。
senses.why: Sport turns the blocking object into a designed test that must be jumped rather than removed.
senses.whyCN: 体育把挡路的物体变成设计好的考验：必须跳过，而不是搬走。

senses.title: A defensive barrier in warfare
senses.definition: a barricade, wire or ditch built to slow an advancing force
senses.definitionCN: 为迟滞对方推进而设置的路障、铁丝网或壕沟
senses.example: Engineers laid an obstacle belt before the position.
senses.exampleCN: 工兵在阵地前布设了一条障碍带。
senses.why: Here the obstacle is deliberately placed by the defender, so blocking becomes a tactic.
senses.whyCN: 这里的障碍由防守方故意设置，阻挡因此成为一种战术。

senses.title: A barrier to communication
senses.definition: a difference of language, culture or channel that keeps a message from arriving
senses.definitionCN: 语言、文化或渠道差异使信息无法抵达
senses.example: Poor translation created an obstacle between the two delegations.
senses.exampleCN: 糟糕的翻译在两个代表团之间造成了障碍。
senses.why: The thing in the way is now a gap in understanding rather than a stone.
senses.whyCN: 此时挡路的不再是石头，而是理解上的缺口。

senses.title: A mental barrier
senses.definition: an inner fear or belief that stops a person from acting
senses.definitionCN: 阻止人行动的内在恐惧或信念
senses.example: Fear of failure was the real obstacle, not the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 真正的障碍是对失败的恐惧，而不是考试。
senses.why: The stone moves inside the mind; the word follows it there.
senses.whyCN: 石头移进了心里；这个词也跟着去了那里。

senses.title: An economic or trade barrier
senses.definition: a tariff, quota or regulation that restricts the movement of goods
senses.definitionCN: 限制商品流动的关税、配额或法规
senses.example: The new tariff became an obstacle to exports.
senses.exampleCN: 新关税成了出口的障碍。
senses.why: Policy builds invisible walls, and the old stone word still fits them.
senses.whyCN: 政策筑起看不见的墙，这个古老的石头词依然适用。

senses.title: The sticking point in a negotiation
senses.definition: the one issue on which talks cannot move forward
senses.definitionCN: 使谈判无法推进的那一个议题
senses.example: Payment terms remained the chief obstacle to the deal.
senses.exampleCN: 付款条件仍是这笔交易的主要症结。
senses.why: In a room of words, one unresolved point can stand in the road like a boulder.
senses.whyCN: 在一屋子言辞里，一个未解决的议题也能像巨石一样横在路上。

senses.title: An object a machine must avoid
senses.titleCN: 机器必须避开的障碍物
senses.definition: an object detected by a vehicle or robot that must be routed around
senses.definitionCN: 车辆或机器人检测到、必须绕开的物体
senses.example: The robot stopped when its sensor detected an obstacle.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器检测到障碍物时，机器人停了下来。
senses.why: Robotics borrowed the plain physical sense and gave it a detection routine.
senses.whyCN: 机器人学借用了最朴素的物理义，并给它配上一套检测程序。

intro.en: Obstacle is a Latin verb for standing against, turned into a noun for the thing that stands in the way; English took it through French.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语表示「站在对面」的动词，转为指「挡在路上的东西」的名词；英语经法语借入。

items.en: stare meant to stand, to remain in place; it is the root of a large family of standing words.
items.cn: stare 意为「站立、留在原地」，是一大类「站立」词的词根。

items.en: ob- meant against, in front of, or towards, and it fixes the direction of the standing.
items.cn: ob- 意为「对着、在前面、朝向」，它规定了「站」的方向。

items.en: obstare was to stand in front of a person or thing, hence to hinder.
items.cn: obstare 意为「站在某人或某物前面」，因此引申为「阻碍」。

items.en: The noun obstaculum named the thing that stands in the way, not the act of standing.
items.cn: 名词 obstaculum 指挡在路上的那个东西，而不是「站」这个动作。

items.en: Old French obstacle carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century; the first date is approximate but the line is clear.
items.cn: 古法语 obstacle 在十四世纪把这个名词带进英语；首见年份为约数，但来源线索清楚。

items.en: Sport, trade, psychology and robotics each reused the stone-in-the-road image for a barrier of their own kind.
items.cn: 体育、贸易、心理学与机器人学各自把「路上的石头」这一意象用于本领域的壁垒。

note.en: The first group shares the standing root or looks close; the second group names nearby barriers and distinguishes how each one blocks.
note.cn: 第一组共享「站立」词根或形音相近；第二组是邻近的阻碍类词，说明中区分各自的阻挡方式。

entries.definition: Stubbornly refusing to change; it uses the same standing-against root for a person's will.
entries.definitionCN: 指固执地拒绝改变；用同一「站着对抗」词根来描述人的意志。

entries.definition: The medical field of childbirth; its Latin source named a midwife as one who stands before the mother.
entries.definitionCN: 指产科医学；其拉丁来源把助产士称为「站在母亲前面的人」。

entries.definition: To block or get in the way; it looks related but is built on a root meaning to pile up, not to stand.
entries.definitionCN: 指阻塞或挡路；形近，但其词根意为「堆起」，而非「站立」。

entries.definition: Several things standing in the way at once.
entries.definitionCN: 指同时挡在路上的多件东西。

entries.definition: A structure or rule that keeps things apart; it separates rather than merely blocking a route.
entries.definitionCN: 指把事物隔开的结构或规则；它重在分隔，而不只是挡住路线。

entries.definition: A small barrier to jump over, or a difficulty to pass; it suggests a sequence of tests.
entries.definitionCN: 指需跳过的矮栏，或需通过的难关；暗示一连串考验。

entries.definition: Something that slows progress, often a defect or burden carried along.
entries.definitionCN: 指拖慢进展的东西，常是随身带着的缺陷或负担。

entries.definition: An outside force crossing into a process and disturbing it; it acts on the process, not on the road.
entries.definitionCN: 指外部力量横插进一个过程并加以扰乱；它作用于过程，而非挡在路上。

entries.definition: A brake applied from inside a person or system; it restrains rather than stands in front.
entries.definitionCN: 指从人或系统内部施加的刹车；它重在拉住，而非立在前面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin stand-against image, the real sport and trade phrases, and the real sister roots.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「站着对抗」意象、真实的体育与贸易搭配，以及真实的同根词。

normal.en: ob- is against and stare is stand: an obstacle is something standing against your path.
normal.cn: ob- 是对着，stare 是站立：障碍就是立在路对面挡住你的东西。

normal.en: The word is a noun for the stone, not for the walking; remove the object and the road reopens.
normal.cn: 这个词是那块石头的名词，不是走路的名词；搬走物体，路就重新打开。

normal.en: Obstacle course and obstacle race are two real sporting phrases.
normal.cn: 障碍赛道与障碍赛是两个真实的体育说法。

normal.en: A trade tariff is an invisible obstacle, but the geometry is the same.
normal.cn: 贸易关税是一道看不见的障碍，但几何关系完全相同。

normal.en: A robot detects an obstacle and routes around it, which is the plain sense in a machine.
normal.cn: 机器人检测到障碍物并绕行，这就是这个词在机器里的朴素用法。

abstract.en: An obstacle is defined by the direction you want to go; the same stone is scenery to a walker heading elsewhere.
abstract.cn: 障碍是由你想去的方向定义的；同一块石头，对朝别处走的行人只是风景。

abstract.en: Some obstacles are placed on purpose, and some are only feared; both stop the feet.
abstract.cn: 有些障碍是故意设置的，有些只存在于恐惧中；两者都能让脚停住。

abstract.en: The word is not an enemy but a test of route: every path proves itself by what it goes around.
abstract.cn: 这个词不是敌人，而是对路线的检验：每条路都用它绕开的东西证明自己。

examples.en: The fallen bridge was the last obstacle between the village and the hospital.
examples.cn: 断桥是村庄与医院之间的最后一道障碍。

examples.en: High interest rates remain an obstacle to small businesses.
examples.cn: 高利率仍是小企业的障碍。

examples.en: The negotiators cleared the main obstacle with a single compromise.
examples.cn: 谈判者用一次妥协清除了主要症结。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「奥布斯脱克」——有东西「站在对面」挡着路

root: 来自拉丁语 obstaculum「阻碍物」← obstare「站在前面阻挡」← ob-「对着、在前」+ stare「站立」；经古法语 obstacle 于十四世纪进入英语。词源链清楚，首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from a stone in the road through abstract hindrance, sport, warfare, language, mind, trade and negotiation to a robot's detected object.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从路上的一块石头，经过抽象阻碍、体育、战争、语言、心智、贸易与谈判，最后落到机器人检测到的物体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boulder sits across a narrow path, and every walker must squeeze past its edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块巨石横在窄路上，每个行人都要从它边缘挤过去。

branches.en: THE STONE AND THE WIRE: a physical object, whether natural or built for defence.
branches.cn: 石头与铁丝：自然存在的实物，或为防御而设的实物。

branches.en: THE RULE AND THE TARIFF: an abstract condition or a policy wall in the way.
branches.cn: 规则与关税：抽象条件或政策之墙挡在路上。

branches.en: THE HURDLE AND THE SENSOR: an obstacle designed for sport or detected by a machine.
branches.cn: 栏架与传感器：为体育设计的障碍，或被机器检测到的障碍。

branches.en: THE WORD AND THE FEAR: a gap in understanding or a belief that stops the feet.
branches.cn: 话语与恐惧：理解上的缺口，或阻止脚步的信念。

branches.en: THE STICKING POINT: one unresolved issue that holds a whole deal in place.
branches.cn: 症结：一个未解决的议题把整笔交易卡住。

intro.en: Obstacle is a prepositional prefix plus a verb of standing plus a noun ending for a thing.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个方位前缀、一个「站立」动词，再加一个表「物」的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies stare, obstare and obstaculum; the English noun came through Old French with the same pieces.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 stare、obstare 与 obstaculum；英语名词经古法语而来，构件相同。

items.example: It fixes the direction of the standing.
The root names a body in place.
items.exampleCN: 词根命名一个立在原地的身体。

items.example: Prefix and root form the key verb.
items.exampleCN: 前缀与词根合成关键动词。

items.example: The noun names the thing, not the act.
It turns the verb into a concrete noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成具体名词。

items.example: The borrowed noun keeps the stone image.
items.exampleCN: 借入的名词保留石头意象。

items.example: The compound adds a designed route.
items.exampleCN: 复合词加上一条设计好的路线。

items.example: A sister word applies the root to the will.
items.exampleCN: 同根词把这个词根用于意志。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加路线名词构成的复合说法，义为「障碍赛道」
由本词加比赛名词构成的复合说法，义为「障碍赛」
本词复数，义为「多处障碍」

definition_zh: 奇怪的；特有的；专属的；有点不舒服的
definition_en: strange or unusual in a way that is hard to explain; belonging only to one person or thing; or, in British informal use, feeling slightly unwell
core_image: 一把只配一把锁的旧钥匙，齿形古怪得让人多看两眼
scene: 旧货摊的角落里躺着一只木盒，锁孔的形状歪歪扭扭，摊主说整条街只有一把钥匙能开它。 There was a peculiar smell in the attic, like old paper and rain.
sceneCN: 这里是「奇怪的」（第 1 个义项：说不清理由地反常）；句意是阁楼里有一股怪味，像旧纸混着雨水。画面里有旧货摊、歪斜的锁孔与积尘的阁楼。

pos.zh: 奇怪的；特有的；专属的；有点不舒服的

derivatives.zh: 由 peculiar 加 -ity 构成，义为「古怪之处；特性」
由 peculiar 加 -ly 构成，义为「奇怪地；尤其」
由 peculiar 与 looking 复合而成，义为「模样古怪的」

senses.title: Strange in a way that is hard to explain
senses.definition: unusual or odd in a way that makes people look twice and wonder why
senses.definitionCN: 反常或古怪到让人多看一眼、想不出原因的程度
senses.example: A peculiar noise came from the empty room.
senses.exampleCN: 空房间里传来一阵怪声。
senses.why: Latin peculiaris first meant belonging to one person alone, and what belongs to one place or one owner soon looks unlike everything around it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 peculiaris 最初意为只属于某一个人，而只属于某一地或某一主人的东西，很快就在周围显得与众不同。

senses.title: Belonging only to one person or thing
senses.definition: existing only in one particular place, group or thing and nowhere else
senses.definitionCN: 只存在于某一地点、群体或事物之中，别处没有
senses.example: This custom is peculiar to the island.
senses.exampleCN: 这种习俗是这个岛所特有的。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is ownership, and ownership is exactly what the phrase peculiar to still states: this belongs here and to nobody else.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层是「归谁所有」，而 peculiar to 这个说法说的正是这一点：它属于这里，不属于别处。

senses.title: Feeling slightly unwell
senses.definition: feeling slightly ill or strange in the body, used in informal British speech
senses.definitionCN: 在英式口语中表示身体略有不适或感觉异样
senses.example: I felt peculiar after the second cup of coffee.
senses.exampleCN: 喝完第二杯咖啡后我觉得有点不舒服。
senses.why: When the body is not its usual self, the feeling is also hard to name, so informal English reaches for the word that already means not quite right.
senses.whyCN: 当身体不在平常状态时，这种感觉也难以命名，于是口语就借用了本来就表示「不太对劲」的那个词。

intro.en: Peculiar begins with cattle: a Latin word for livestock became a word for private property, then for what belongs to one owner, and finally for what looks odd to everyone else.
intro.cn: peculiar 从牲畜讲起：拉丁语中表示家畜的词先变成「私产」，再指只属于某一主人的东西，最后指在别人眼里古怪的东西。

items.en: Pecus meant cattle, and in an economy counted in herds, livestock were the clearest visible form of wealth.
items.cn: pecus 意为牛群牲畜；在以牲畜计财的经济里，牲畜就是最清楚可见的财富形式。

items.en: Peculium was the private savings that a person, often a slave, could hold as personal property.
items.cn: peculium 指个人（常是奴隶）可以持有的私产积蓄。

items.en: Peculiaris meant belonging to one person rather than to the community, so it began as a word about ownership.
items.cn: peculiaris 意为属于某个人而非集体，所以它最初是一个谈归属的词。

items.en: Old French peculier passed the adjective into English with the sense of a possession or right that belonged to one party alone.
items.cn: 古法语 peculier 把这个形容词传入英语，指只属于一方的财物或权利。

items.en: Modern English widened the adjective from private ownership to anything marked as special, and then to what strikes us as odd.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个形容词从私人所有扩展到任何带有特殊标记的事物，再扩展到让人觉得古怪的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same Latin stem of private property; the near-meaning group collects adjectives for what is unusual or typical of one thing.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一「私产」拉丁词干上的词；近义组收表示反常或为某物所典型的形容词。

entries.definition: A strange detail, or the quality of belonging to one thing only.
entries.definitionCN: 奇怪的细节；或只属于某一事物的特性。

entries.definition: In a strange way, or in a way special to one person.
entries.definitionCN: 以奇怪的方式；或以某人特有的方式。

entries.definition: Connected with money, from the same Latin word for wealth.
entries.definitionCN: 与金钱有关的，来自同一个表示财富的拉丁词。

entries.definition: Unusual or surprising in a way that is hard to explain.
entries.definitionCN: 不寻常或令人惊讶、难以解释的。

entries.definition: Different from what is expected; slightly strange.
entries.definitionCN: 与预期不同、有些古怪的。

entries.definition: Strange in an interesting way, or eager to know something.
Typical of a particular person or thing.
entries.definitionCN: 某一人物或事物所典型的。

normalIntro.en: A word about property turned into a word about oddity, and both meanings are still visible in its family.
normalIntro.cn: 一个谈财产的词后来变成谈古怪的词，而两层意思至今都能在它的词族里看见。

normal.en: Peculiar begins with cattle: Latin pecus gave wealth, and wealth gave the idea of property.
normal.cn: peculiar 从牲畜讲起：拉丁语 pecus 带来财富，财富又带来「财产」的观念。

normal.en: Peculium was private savings, so peculiaris meant belonging to one owner rather than to everyone.
normal.cn: peculium 是私产积蓄，所以 peculiaris 意为属于某个主人，而不是属于所有人。

normal.en: Peculiar to still keeps the old ownership sense, as in a bird peculiar to one island.
normal.cn: peculiar to 仍保留旧的归属义，例如只属于某一岛的鸟。

normal.en: The modern sense of odd grew from marking something as special, since what is special stands out from the ordinary.
normal.cn: 现代的「古怪」义从「标记为特殊」发展而来，因为特殊的东西总会从平常中显出来。

normal.en: Peculiarity and peculiarly keep the stem unchanged before the endings, with no letter dropped.
normal.cn: peculiarity 与 peculiarly 在接词尾时词干不变，也没有字母脱落。

abstract.en: Peculiar says two things at once: this belongs only here, and this does not fit everywhere else.
abstract.cn: peculiar 同时说两件事：它只属于这里，而它在别处并不合身。

abstract.en: A word born from private property now describes a private oddity, which is a small history of ownership.
abstract.cn: 一个从私产诞生的词如今描述私人的古怪，这本身就是一部小小的所有权史。

abstract.en: What is peculiar is not wrong, only marked; the word leaves room for both charm and unease.
abstract.cn: 古怪并不等于错误，只是被做了标记；这个词同时留着迷人不安两种余地。

examples.en: There was a peculiar smell in the attic.
examples.cn: 阁楼里有一股怪味。

examples.en: This bird is peculiar to the island and lives nowhere else.
examples.cn: 这种鸟为该岛所特有，别处没有。

examples.en: He looked at me in a peculiar way and said nothing.
examples.cn: 他用古怪的眼神看着我，一言不发。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮酷」——奇怪的皮具酷得让人多看两眼；peculiar 就是奇怪的。

root: 来自拉丁语 peculium（私产、积蓄），其源头是 pecus（牲畜）；peculiaris 意为「属于某个人的」，后经古法语 peculier 进入英语，词义从「专属」扩展到「特有」与「古怪」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is what belongs to one owner only; the senses run from private ownership to what is special to a place, and then to what looks odd because it belongs nowhere else.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是只属于某一主人的东西；义项从私人所有，到某地特有，再到因为不合于别处而显得古怪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old key whose teeth are cut for one lock only, so everyone else finds it odd.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把只为一把锁磨出的旧钥匙，在别人眼里显得古怪。

branches.en: an attic where an unknown smell hangs in the air
branches.cn: 阁楼里说不清来源的气味

branches.en: a bird found on one island and nowhere else
branches.cn: 只在一座岛上才能见到的鸟

branches.en: a man who feels unwell after a second cup of coffee
branches.cn: 喝了第二杯咖啡后觉得不适的人

branches.en: a thing that belongs to one place and a body that does not feel itself
branches.cn: 一件只属于某地的东西，与一具不在常态的身体

branches.en: what is special to one place and what is odd to everyone
branches.cn: 对某地特有之物，与让所有人觉得古怪之物

intro.en: A Latin word for cattle lies under this adjective, and the chain of property words built on it still explains why special and strange share one form.
intro.cn: 这个形容词底下是一个表示牲畜的拉丁词，建立在它之上的财产词链至今解释了为何「特有」与「古怪」共用一个形式。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 发光；光辉；容光
definition_en: to give off a steady light, a soft radiance, or a warm feeling
core_image: 壁炉里的余烬仍然发着暗红的光
scene: 炉火在壁炉里发出红光。 The fire glowed in the hearth.
sceneCN: 这里 glow 是「发光」（第 1 个义项）；句意：炉火在壁炉里发出红光。

derivatives.zh: 发光的；热情的
热情洋溢地
余晖；余味

senses.title: To give off light
senses.definition: to send out a steady light and heat without flames
senses.definitionCN: 没有火焰却持续发出光和热
senses.example: The fire glowed in the hearth.
senses.exampleCN: 炉火在壁炉里发出红光。
senses.why: This is the physical sense at the centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最核心的物理含义。

senses.title: A soft radiance
senses.definition: a steady, soft light
senses.definitionCN: 稳定而柔和的光
senses.example: The glow of the lamp filled the room.
senses.exampleCN: 灯光充满了房间。
senses.why: The noun names the light that the verb produces.
senses.whyCN: 名词命名动词所产生的光。

senses.title: A warm feeling

items.en: The word extended to the warmth of health and feeling.

normalIntro.cn: glow 是留下来、会呼吸的光。

normal.en: The fire glowed in the hearth.

normal.en: The glow of the lamp filled the room.
normal.cn: 灯光充满了房间。

normal.en: Her face had a healthy glow.

normal.en: The stars glowed above the lake.
normal.cn: 星星在湖面上方闪烁。

normal.en: He glowed with pride at the news.

abstract.en: Glow is what fire leaves when it chooses to stay.
abstract.cn: glow 是火选择留下时留下的东西。

abstract.en: A quiet glow outlasts a bright flame.

abstract.en: People glow when they are fully themselves.
abstract.cn: 人做回自己时，会发光。

root: 来自古英语 glowan（发光、发热），属日耳曼语族，核心义由无焰燃烧的光扩展到面色与情感的光彩。

sensesIntro.en: Glow means to give off steady light, the light itself, or a warm look of feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: glow 意为持续发光、所发之光，或情感流露的暖色。

core.en: Heat that shines without a flame.
core.cn: 没有火焰却在发亮的热。

branches.en: Embers breathe red in a fireplace.
branches.cn: 余烬在壁炉里透出红色。

branches.en: A lamp fills a room with soft light.
branches.cn: 一盏灯用柔光充满房间。

branches.en: A face shines after good news.
branches.cn: 听到好消息，脸上一亮。

branches.en: The act and the light are one warmth.
branches.cn: 发光的动作与光，是同一份温暖。

branches.en: Outer light is a picture of inner warmth.
branches.cn: 外在的光，是内在温暖的写照。

intro.en: Glow forms verbs, adjectives, and compounds.
intro.cn: glow 构成动词、形容词和复合词。

latinIntro.en: Glow has no Latin root; it comes from Old English glowan.

definition_zh: 逐渐的；渐进的；平缓的
definition_en: happening slowly by small steps, or not steep
core_image: 清晨的光一点点爬上窗台，阴影缓慢后退，没有一处骤变
scene: 天气逐渐转暖。 The weather showed a gradual warming.
sceneCN: 这里 gradual 是「逐渐的、渐进的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：天气逐渐转暖。

derivatives.zh: 逐渐地
渐进性；逐渐

senses.title: Step by step
senses.definition: happening slowly in small stages
senses.definitionCN: 以小的阶段缓慢发生
senses.example: The weather showed a gradual warming.
senses.exampleCN: 天气逐渐转暖。
senses.why: This is the central sense of change by small steps.
senses.whyCN: 这是以小步变化的核心含义。

senses.title: Not steep
senses.definition: rising or falling gently, not sharply
senses.definitionCN: 平缓升降，而非陡峭
senses.example: The hill has a gradual slope.
senses.exampleCN: 这座山坡度平缓。
senses.why: A gentle slope is a stair whose steps are almost level.
senses.whyCN: 平缓的坡，是几乎水平的台阶。

senses.title: Slow to finish
senses.definition: happening slowly over a long time
senses.definitionCN: 在长时间内缓慢发生
senses.example: Her recovery was gradual but steady.
senses.exampleCN: 她的康复缓慢但稳定。
senses.why: Step-by-step progress is experienced as slowness.
senses.whyCN: 一步一的进展，被体验为缓慢。

intro.en: Gradual came from medieval Latin gradualis, of steps.
intro.cn: gradual 来自中世纪拉丁语 gradualis，意为台阶的。

items.en: Gradus meant a step.
items.cn: gradus 意为台阶。

items.en: Gradualis meant arranged by steps.
items.cn: gradualis 意为按台阶排列的。

items.en: Gradual entered English meaning by small degrees.
items.cn: gradual 以按小等级变化之义进入英语。

items.en: It described slow change of any kind.
items.cn: 它描述任何种类的缓慢变化。

items.en: It also described gentle slopes.
items.cn: 它也用来描述平缓的坡。

note.en: Gradual is compared with look-alike words and words for slowness.
note.cn: 把 gradual 与形近词以及表示缓慢的词作比较。

entries.definition: a person who has finished study
thankful

happening in stages

normalIntro.en: Gradual is change that climbs one small step at a time.
normalIntro.cn: gradual 是一次只爬一级台阶的变化。

normal.en: The weather showed a gradual warming.
normal.cn: 天气逐渐转暖。

normal.en: The hill has a gradual slope.
normal.cn: 这座山坡度平缓。

normal.en: Her recovery was gradual but steady.
normal.cn: 她的康复缓慢但稳定。

normal.en: There was a gradual increase in prices.
normal.cn: 价格逐渐上涨。

normal.en: Learning a language is a gradual process.
normal.cn: 学一门语言是渐进的过程。

abstract.en: Gradual change is invisible until it is complete.
abstract.cn: 渐变在完成之前都看不见。

abstract.en: The steepest fall is made of gentle steps.
abstract.cn: 最陡的坠落由平缓的台阶组成。

abstract.en: What happens gradually cannot be undone at once.
abstract.cn: 逐渐发生的事，无法一下子撤销。

examples.en: The weather showed a gradual warming.
examples.cn: 天气逐渐转暖。

examples.en: The hill has a gradual slope.
examples.cn: 这座山坡度平缓。

examples.en: Her recovery was gradual but steady.
examples.cn: 她的康复缓慢但稳定。

dict_mnemonic.text: gradual 源自拉丁语 gradus（台阶），表示「一步一步的、逐渐的」，也可形容坡度平缓；副词 gradually 是「逐渐地」，gradual change 是「逐渐的变化」，与 grade（等级）、graduate（毕业）同根。

root: 来自中世纪拉丁语 gradualis，源于拉丁语 gradus（台阶），本义为按台阶排列的，引申为逐渐的、渐进的与坡度平缓的。

sensesIntro.en: Gradual means happening by small steps, gently sloping, or slow over time.
sensesIntro.cn: gradual 指以小步逐渐发生、坡度平缓，或在长时间内缓慢。

core.en: Change taken one step at a time.
core.cn: 一次一级台阶的变化。

branches.en: Warmth seeps in without a single jolt.
branches.cn: 暖意渗入，没有一次骤变。

branches.en: A hill rises so gently you hardly notice.
branches.cn: 山坡缓缓升起，几乎察觉不到。

branches.en: A patient improves a little each week.
branches.cn: 病人每周好转一点。

branches.en: Many small steps look like slowness from afar.
branches.cn: 许多小步从远处看就像缓慢。

branches.en: A gentle slope and a slow recovery share one measure.
branches.cn: 平缓的坡与缓慢的康复共用一种尺度。

intro.en: Gradual forms adverbs and nouns of slow change.
intro.cn: gradual 构成表示缓慢变化的副词和名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is gradus, a step, with the adjective ending -alis.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 gradus（台阶），带形容词词尾 -alis。

definition_zh: 侵略；侵入；侵扰；侵犯
definition_en: to enter a country or place by force, or to enter somewhere in large numbers where one is not wanted
core_image: 军队越过界碑，旗帜插进对方的土地
scene: 海面上排开许多小船，天未亮就往沙滩方向划来。 Tourists invade the small town every August.
sceneCN: 这里 invade 是「涌入、侵扰」（第 2 个义项：大批进入不受欢迎的地方），句意为每年八月游客涌入这座小镇。画面里的物件：小船、沙滩、界碑。

pos.zh: 动词：侵略；侵入；侵扰；侵犯

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -sion 构成，义为「侵略；侵扰」
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「入侵者」
由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「侵入的；扩散性的」
同一词根 vadere 构成，义为「逃避」

senses.title: Enter by force
senses.definition: to enter a country or region with armed force in order to conquer it
senses.definitionCN: 以武力进入一国或地区以图征服
senses.example: The army invaded the province at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 军队在黎明时入侵了那个省。
senses.why: Latin vadere means to go; in- means into, so the word is simply to go in.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vadere 意为「走」，in- 意为「进入」，所以本义就是「走进去」。

senses.title: Arrive in crowds
senses.definition: to enter a place in large numbers, often where people do not welcome it
senses.definitionCN: 大批进入某地，且往往不受欢迎
senses.example: Fans invaded the field in the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一分钟球迷涌进了球场。
senses.why: The force of the verb softened into sheer numbers.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词的力量感弱化成了「人多」。

senses.title: Trespass on rights or privacy
senses.definition: to intrude on someone's privacy, rights, or personal space
senses.definitionCN: 侵入他人的隐私、权利或个人空间
senses.example: Constant calls invaded what was left of her evening.
senses.exampleCN: 不断的电话侵占了她仅剩的夜晚。
senses.why: Borders can be personal, so invasion moves from land to rights.
senses.whyCN: 界线也可以是个人的，于是「入侵」从土地移到权利。

senses.title: Spread where unwanted
senses.definition: to spread through a body, an environment, or a market where it does harm
senses.definitionCN: 在身体、环境或市场中扩散并造成损害
senses.example: A weed from Asia invaded the riverbanks.
senses.exampleCN: 一种来自亚洲的杂草侵占了河岸。
senses.why: Plants and cells obey the same picture: going where they were not invited.
senses.whyCN: 植物与细胞遵循同一图像：去到自己没被邀请的地方。

intro.en: Invade comes from Latin invadere, to go into, from in- "into" and vadere "to go".
intro.cn: invade 来自拉丁语 invadere「走进去」，由 in-「进入」与 vadere「走」构成。

items.en: Vadere meant to go or to walk forward.
items.cn: vadere 意为行走或向前走。

items.en: Invadere meant to go in, especially with force.
items.cn: invadere 意为走进去，尤指强行进入。

items.en: The noun invasio named a hostile entry.
items.cn: 名词 invasio 指敌意的进入。

items.en: French envahir carried the military sense into English.
items.cn: 法语 envahir 把军事义带入英语。

items.en: The word came to cover crowds, privacy, and disease.
items.cn: 这个词后来覆盖了人群、隐私与疾病。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -vade going root; the near-meaning group holds other words for breaking in.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -vade「走」词根；近义组收其他表示「闯入」的词。

entries.definition: The act or event of invading.
To get away from something by dodging.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「逃避」，同出 vadere。

entries.definition: An armed or unwelcome intruder.
To enter where one is not welcome or expected.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「闯入」，更强调冒犯。

entries.definition: To take and hold a place by force.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「占领」，强调控制而非进入。

entries.definition: A short sudden attack on a place.

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the picture of a border crossed without permission.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子守着「一条界线被人不经允许踩过」的画面。

normal.en: in- into plus vadere go equals go into, uninvited.
normal.cn: in-「进入」加 vadere「走」等于未经邀请地走进去。

normal.en: The same going root is inside evade, to go away from trouble.
normal.cn: 同一个「走」的词根藏在 evade 里，那是往麻烦外走。

normal.en: Tourists can invade a town without a single soldier.
normal.cn: 不用一个兵，游客也能侵占一座小镇。

normal.en: Privacy can be invaded by a phone call.
normal.cn: 隐私可以被一通电话侵占。

normal.en: Add -sion and invasion is the event, not the act.
normal.cn: 加 -sion 成 invasion，指那个事件。

abstract.en: To invade is to treat a boundary as a suggestion.
abstract.cn: 入侵是把一条界线当成建议。

abstract.en: Weeds and armies move in the same direction.
abstract.cn: 杂草和军队朝同一个方向推进。

abstract.en: Every invasion begins with a step someone thought was allowed.
abstract.cn: 每次入侵都始于某个自认为被允许的脚步。

examples.en: Neighbours invaded the garden with their footballs every weekend.
examples.cn: 每到周末，邻家孩子就带着足球闯进花园。

examples.en: The company invaded a market long held by two rivals.
examples.cn: 这家公司打入了一个长期由两家对手占据的市场。

examples.en: Reporters must be careful not to invade private grief.
examples.cn: 记者必须小心，别去侵扰别人的私人之痛。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（进入）+ vade（走）——径直走进去

root: 拉丁语 vadere「走」→ invadere「强行走入」→ invasio「入侵」→ 古法语 envahir → 英语 invade。同族有 invasion、invader、evade。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: armed entry, crowds arriving, trespass on privacy, and harmful spread.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：武力进入、人群涌入、侵犯隐私，以及有害的蔓延。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: boots stepping across a boundary stone.
core.cn: 核心意象：靴子踩过一块界石。

branches.en: THE ARMY: armed entry across a national border.
branches.cn: 军队这条线：越过国界的武装进入。

branches.en: THE STADIUM: crowds pouring over the rail.
branches.cn: 球场这条线：人群翻过栏杆涌入。

branches.en: THE PHONE: a call that takes a private evening.
branches.cn: 电话这条线：吞掉私人夜晚的来电。

branches.en: THE WEED: a plant colonising a riverbank.
branches.cn: 杂草这条线：占据河岸的植物。

branches.en: THE LINK: both take ground that belonged to others.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都占有了别人的地方。

intro.en: Invade is in- "into" plus the Latin root vad- "go" with a verb ending.
intro.cn: invade 是 in-「进入」加拉丁词根 vad-「走」与动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin vadere and invadere are recorded; the family also gives English evade.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vadere 与 invadere 均有记载，这一族也给英语带来 evade。

items.example: It marks the direction of travel.
The root also lives in evade and pervasive.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也见于 evade 与 pervasive。

items.example: The verb is the base of the root.
The verb is the direct source.
It forms evade, to go out of reach.

definition_zh: 接收器；收件人；听筒
definition_en: a device that picks up signals; a person who receives something; the part of a telephone held to the ear
core_image: 一只黑色盒子接着天线，指示灯亮起
scene: 桌上摆着一台老式收音机，金属旋钮旁的天线伸向窗外。 He adjusted the receiver to catch a clearer signal.
sceneCN: 这里 receiver 是「接收器」（第 1 个义项：接收信号的设备）；句意为他把接收器调了调，想收到更清楚的信号。画面里可留意：伸向窗外的天线、亮起的指示灯。

derivatives.zh: 收到；接收
接待；接收
应收的

senses.title: A device that picks up signals
senses.definition: an apparatus that catches and turns broadcast or electronic signals into sound or pictures
senses.definitionCN: 捕捉广播或电子信号并转成声音或图像的装置
senses.example: He adjusted the receiver to catch a clearer signal.
senses.exampleCN: 他把接收器调了调，想收到更清楚的信号。
senses.why: The suffix -er marks the doer, so a device that receives takes the same name as a person who receives.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -er 标记施动者，因此执行接收的设备与执行接收的人共用一个名称。

senses.title: A person who receives
senses.definition: a person to whom something is sent or given
senses.definitionCN: 某物被寄送或给予的对象
senses.example: The receiver must sign for the parcel.
senses.exampleCN: 收件人必须在包裹上签字。
senses.why: In law and post, the one who takes delivery is named by the act, and -er turns receive into that name.
senses.whyCN: -er 把 receive 变成施动名词，在法律与邮政用语中，收货的一方就以此命名。

senses.title: The telephone handset
senses.definition: the part of a telephone that is held to the ear and produces sound
senses.definitionCN: 电话中贴近耳朵并发出声音的部分
senses.example: She lifted the receiver and heard a dial tone.
senses.exampleCN: 她拿起听筒，听到了拨号音。
senses.why: The part held to the ear receives the voice, so the device took the name of what it does.
senses.whyCN: 贴近耳朵的部分负责接收声音，于是这件器件以其功能得名。

intro.en: Receiver is receive plus the agent suffix -er, and the same pattern names a machine, a person, and a telephone part.
intro.cn: receiver 是 receive 加施动后缀 -er，同一构词方式命名了机器、人，以及电话部件。

items.en: Recipere, to receive, came to English through French as receive.
items.cn: recipere（接收）经法语进入英语，成为 receive。

items.en: The native suffix -er marks the one who performs an action, giving receiver.
items.cn: 本族后缀 -er 标记执行动作的一方，由此构成 receiver。

items.en: Middle English receivere named a person who took something in.
items.cn: 中古英语 receivere 指收下某物的人。

items.en: With the telephone, the part held to the ear was called the receiver.
items.cn: 随着电话出现，贴近耳朵的部件被称为 receiver。

items.en: Radio and satellite sets borrowed the same word for the unit that catches signals.
items.cn: 收音机与卫星设备借用同一个词，指捕捉信号的装置。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers agent nouns from the same verb family; the near-meaning group gathers words for recipients and devices.
note.cn: 形近组收同一动词族里的施动名词；近义组收表收件人与设备的词。

entries.definition: A person who misleads others.
A person who notices things.
A person who forms an idea.
One who receives something.
The part of a phone held in the hand.
One who gathers things.
