normalIntro.en: The word is receive plus -er: whatever does the receiving, person or machine, is a receiver.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 receive 加 -er：无论人或机器，只要做接收这件事，就是 receiver。

normal.en: Receive plus -er: the one that receives.
normal.cn: receive 加 -er：接收的那一方。

normal.en: A radio receiver catches signals; a telephone receiver catches a voice.
normal.cn: radio receiver 接收信号，telephone receiver 接收声音。

normal.en: A receiver of stolen goods is a person, not a machine.
normal.cn: receiver of stolen goods 指的是人，不是机器。

normal.en: The plural is receivers, with no change in the base.
normal.cn: 复数是 receivers，词干不变。

normal.en: Keep the ei in receive and the -er on the end.
normal.cn: 记住 receive 里的 ei 与词尾的 -er。

abstract.en: Every receiver defines a sender; the two are made for each other.
abstract.cn: 每一个接收者都定义了一个发送者，两者互为存在。

abstract.en: A receiver is powerful only when it is tuned to the right wave.
abstract.cn: 接收器只有调到正确的波长才有力量。

abstract.en: To be a receiver of kindness is to owe a return that may never come.
abstract.cn: 接受善意的人，欠下了一份也许永远不必偿还的回报。

examples.en: He adjusted the receiver to catch a clearer signal.
examples.cn: 他把接收器调了调，想收到更清楚的信号。

examples.en: The receiver must sign for the parcel.
examples.cn: 收件人必须在包裹上签字。

examples.en: She lifted the receiver and heard a dial tone.
examples.cn: 她拿起听筒，听到了拨号音。

dict_mnemonic.text: receive（接收）加 er（做某事的人或物）：会接收的东西就是接收器，接收的人就是收件人，电话上接收声音的就是听筒。

root: receive（收到）加后缀 -er（表施动者或工具）→ receiver；receive 源自拉丁 recipere；同族有 reception、receivable。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the one that receives; the senses split into a machine, a person, and a telephone part.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「负责接收的那一方」；义项分为机器、人，以及电话部件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a black box with an aerial, its indicator light glowing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只接着天线的黑盒子，指示灯亮起。

branches.en: a box with a glowing lamp
branches.cn: 一只亮着指示灯的盒子

branches.en: a hand signing for a parcel
branches.cn: 一只手在包裹上签字

branches.en: a handset lifted to the ear
branches.cn: 听筒被举到耳边

branches.en: a machine and a person that receive
branches.cn: 接收的机器与接收的人

branches.en: a parcel taken and a voice heard
branches.cn: 收下包裹，也听见声音

intro.en: The word is built with the agent suffix -er on the verb receive, and that shape serves both people and machines.
intro.cn: 这个词由动词 receive 加施动后缀 -er 构成，这一外形同时适用于人与机器。

latinIntro.en: The verb goes back to Latin recipere; the suffix -er is native English.
latinIntro.cn: 动词可追溯到拉丁 recipere；后缀 -er 是英语本族成分。

definition_zh: 伏特；伏；电压单位；（旧）环骑步法
definition_en: a unit of electrical force, defined as the push that moves one ampere through one ohm
core_image: 一节干电池上标着一个数字，指针随之轻轻一摆
scene: 实验课上，老师把万用表接到旧电池两端，读数只剩一点点。 The battery had lost half a volt, so the lamp would not light.
sceneCN: 这里 volt 是「伏特」（第 1 个义项：电压单位）；句意为这节电池少了半伏，灯就点不亮了。表盘上指针轻摆的那一刻就是这个单位在做的事。

derivatives.zh: 由 volt 加 -age 构成，义为「电压」
volt 与 meter（计量器）复合，义为「伏特计；电压表」
volt 与 ampere 复合，义为「伏安」，视在功率单位

senses.title: The unit of electric force
senses.definition: the unit used to measure the force that drives a current in a circuit
senses.definitionCN: 衡量电路中推动电流的力量大小的单位
senses.example: The battery had lost half a volt, so the lamp would not light.
senses.exampleCN: 这节电池少了半伏，灯就点不亮了。
senses.why: The unit is named after Alessandro Volta, who built the first steady source of current; his name became the measure of the push itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个单位以亚历山德罗·伏打命名，他造出第一个稳定的电流源，他的名字就成了「推力」本身的度量。

senses.title: A unit in compound names
senses.definition: used inside larger unit names such as electron volt and kilovolt
senses.definitionCN: 用于电子伏、千伏等更大单位名称之中
senses.example: A kilovolt is a thousand units of electric force.
senses.exampleCN: 一千伏就是电压的一千个单位。
senses.why: A practical unit is too small for power lines and too large for chips, so the word is attached to prefixes.
senses.whyCN: 实用单位对电力线路太小、对芯片又太大，于是这个词被挂上各种前缀。

senses.title: The measured value in speech
senses.definition: the number of volts actually present, as read from a meter
senses.definitionCN: 从表上读出的、实际存在的电压数值
senses.example: The reading dropped to three volts within a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 读数在一分钟内降到三伏。
senses.why: Once the unit exists, people stop saying the unit and just quote the number as a plain count of volts.
senses.whyCN: 单位一旦确立，人们就不再说单位本身，而直接把数值当作伏特的计数来讲。

senses.title: The name of the inventor
senses.definition: the surname of the Italian scientist whose experiments gave electricity a steady push
senses.definitionCN: 意大利科学家的姓氏，他的实验给了电流稳定的推动力
senses.example: Volta showed that two metals and a wet cloth could move a current.
senses.exampleCN: 伏打证明两种金属加一块湿布就能推动电流。
senses.why: Scientific units often borrow the name of the person who made the measurement possible; here the name kept its capital only for the man.
senses.whyCN: 科学单位常借用促成测量之人的名字，这里只有写人时才保留大写。

senses.title: Round in a riding manoeuvre
senses.definition: in older fencing and riding language, a turn or a circular step to one side
senses.definitionCN: 旧时击剑与马术用语里，向一侧的转身或绕行步
senses.example: The rider performed a volt before the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 骑手在门前走了一个环步。
senses.why: This is a separate Italian borrowing from voltare, to turn; only the spelling matches the electrical unit.
senses.whyCN: 这是另从意大利语 voltare（转）借来的词，只是拼写与电压单位相同，来源不同。

intro.en: Volt is a scientist surname turned into a unit; the older riding word is a separate Italian borrowing that happens to look the same.
intro.cn: volt 由科学家姓氏变为单位；较早的马术语则是另一个意大利语借词，只是拼写相同。

items.en: The surname Volta belongs to an Italian family from Como, and its origin is uncertain.
items.cn: Volta 是科莫一户意大利人家的姓氏，来源不确定。

items.en: Alessandro Volta built the pile that produced a steady current, which made exact measurement possible.
items.cn: 亚历山德罗·伏打造出能产生稳定电流的电堆，使精确测量成为可能。

items.en: In the eighteen sixties the international electrical congress adopted volt as the unit of force.
items.cn: 十九世纪六十年代，国际电学会议采用 volt 作为电压单位。

items.en: Prefixed forms such as millivolt and kilovolt spread with telegraphy and power supply.
items.cn: 毫伏、千伏等带前缀形式随电报与供电普及。

items.en: The separate riding term volt entered from French and Italian voltare, to turn, and remains rare.
items.cn: 另一个马术语 volt 来自法语与意大利语 voltare（转），如今很少使用。

note.en: The first group holds the family built on the unit, the second the other electrical measures it works with.
note.cn: 第一组收以该单位为基础的词族，第二组收与它配合的其他电学量度。

entries.definition: The plain plural of the unit.
The noun for the amount of electric force, measured in volts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「电压」，以伏特计量。

entries.definition: An instrument that reads volts directly.
entries.definitionCN: 直接读出伏特数的仪器。

entries.definition: The surname of the Italian scientist behind the unit.
entries.definitionCN: 促成该单位的意大利科学家姓氏。

entries.definition: The unit of current, the flow that a volt drives.
entries.definitionCN: 电流单位，即伏特所推动的流动。

entries.definition: The unit of resistance, opposing that flow.
entries.definitionCN: 电阻单位，阻碍这种流动。

entries.definition: The unit of power, volts times amperes.
entries.definitionCN: 功率单位，等于伏特乘以安培。

entries.definition: The flow of charge itself, measured in amperes.
entries.definitionCN: 电荷流动本身，以安培计量。

normalIntro.en: One name, one unit, and three plain endings carry the whole family.
normalIntro.cn: 一个名字、一个单位，加上三个普通后缀，就撑起整个词族。

normal.en: Volt comes from the surname of Alessandro Volta; it is a name, not a Latin idea.
normal.cn: volt 来自亚历山德罗·伏打的姓氏，是专名而非拉丁义素。

normal.en: Volt measures the push, ampere the flow, ohm the resistance.
normal.cn: volt 量推力，ampere 量流动，ohm 量阻力。

normal.en: Voltage is the amount, volt is the unit; we say a voltage of five volts.
normal.cn: voltage 是量，volt 是单位；说 a voltage of five volts。

normal.en: A voltmeter reads volts; the -meter part means a measuring device.
normal.cn: voltmeter 读伏特，-meter 表示计量器。

normal.en: The plural is volts, with no change to the stem.
normal.cn: 复数是 volts，词干不变。

abstract.en: See a small battery with a printed number on its side.
abstract.cn: 想一节小电池，侧面印着一个数字。

abstract.en: Feel a gentle push travelling through a wire, like water under pressure.
abstract.cn: 感受一股轻推沿导线前行，像有压力的水。

abstract.en: Hear a needle swing and settle on a marked line.
abstract.cn: 听指针摆一下，停在刻度线上。

examples.en: The old radio works on nine volts.
examples.cn: 这台旧收音机用九伏电压工作。

examples.en: A single volt is a very small push for a machine.
examples.cn: 对一台机器来说，一伏是很小的推力。

examples.en: He measured the volt drop across the wire.
examples.cn: 他测了导线两端的电压降。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「沃特」——沃特拿着电池说：电压得按伏特来算。

root: 意大利语姓氏 Volta（亚历山德罗·伏打）→ 英语单位名 volt；姓氏本身的来源不确定。另有马术语 volt 来自意大利语 voltare（转），与电压单位无关。

sensesIntro.en: A surname becomes a unit, then a compound part, then a number people quote, then the man again, and finally a look-alike riding word from another root.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个姓氏变作单位，再做复合单位的一部分、成为人们直接报出的数字、回到那位科学家，最后是与它同形的另一个来源的马术语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one battery and one swinging needle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一节电池与一根摆动的指针。

branches.en: The unit branch: one volt of push through a circuit.
branches.cn: 单位分支：推动电路的一伏。

branches.en: The compound branch: millivolt, kilovolt, electron volt.
branches.cn: 复合分支：毫伏、千伏、电子伏。

branches.en: The reading branch: the meter shows three volts.
branches.cn: 读数分支：表上显示三伏。

branches.en: The person branch: Volta and his pile.
branches.cn: 人物分支：伏打与他的电堆。

branches.en: The riding branch: a turn before the gate.
branches.cn: 马术分支：门前的一次绕行。

intro.en: Volt-, Volta- carry only a name; -age, -meter and -s build the rest.
intro.cn: volt-、volta- 只携带专名信息，-age、-meter、-s 承担其余构词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root meaning electricity here; the family rests on an Italian surname of uncertain origin.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有表示电的拉丁词根，整个词族建立在来源不确定的意大利姓氏上。

items.meaning: the inventor of the electric pile
items.example: Volta taught physics in Como and Pavia.
items.exampleCN: 伏打在科莫与帕维亚教物理学。

items.example: The unit was fixed in his honour.
Volts divided by ohms give amperes.

definition_zh: 小心的；谨慎的；有保留的
definition_en: careful to avoid danger or mistakes, and unwilling to take risks or promise too much
core_image: 伸脚试探地面，先确认再迈步
scene: 新司机第一次上高速。 She was cautious and kept a wide distance from the truck ahead.
sceneCN: 这里 cautious 指「谨慎的」（第 1 个义项：小心避免危险）；句意是她很谨慎，与前方的卡车保持很宽的距离。

pos.zh: 小心的；谨慎的；有保留的

derivatives.zh: 小心；警告
谨慎地
谨慎；慎重

senses.title: Careful to avoid danger
senses.definition: acting with care so as to avoid danger, harm or mistakes
senses.definitionCN: 行事小心，以避免危险、伤害或错误
senses.example: Be cautious when the floor is wet.
senses.exampleCN: 地面湿滑时要小心。
senses.why: The Latin source means to beware, so the adjective describes a person who keeps watch before acting.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源义是当心提防，所以这个形容词形容先看清再行动的人。

senses.title: Guarded in what one says
senses.titleCN: 有保留的；不轻易表态的
senses.definition: refusing to commit fully to an opinion or promise
senses.definitionCN: 不愿完全承诺某个看法或保证
senses.example: The minister gave a cautious welcome to the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 部长对该计划表示有保留的欢迎。
senses.why: If you watch your step, you also watch your words, so caution spreads from movement to speech.
senses.whyCN: 既然会看住脚下的步子，也会看住口中的话，谨慎就从行动蔓延到言语。

intro.en: Cautious is built in English on caution, which comes from a Latin verb meaning to beware.
intro.cn: cautious 是在英语中用 caution 加后缀构成的，而 caution 来自一个意为当心的拉丁语动词。

items.en: Cavere meant to be on guard, to take care or to beware.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cavere 意为提防、当心。

items.en: Cautio, from the same verb, meant a guarding or a written security.
items.cn: 同源的 cautio 意为防范，也指书面担保。

items.en: Caution carried the sense of care and warning into medieval French.
items.cn: 古法语 caution 把小心与警告义带入中世纪法语。

items.en: English forms cautious by adding -ous to caution, meaning full of care.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪给 caution 加 -ous 构成 cautious，意为充满小心。

items.en: Modern usage extends the word to guarded opinions and cautious optimism.
items.cn: 现代用法把该词扩展到有保留的看法与谨慎乐观。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the caution family, while the meaning group lists other careful adjectives.
note.cn: 形近组沿 caution 词族展开，近义组列出其他表示小心的形容词。

entries.definition: great care to avoid danger
entries.definitionCN: 为避免危险而格外小心

entries.definition: in a careful way
the quality of being careful
giving attention to avoid harm or error
watchful because of possible danger
entries.definitionCN: 因可能有危险而保持警觉的

entries.definition: showing good judgement about risk
entries.definitionCN: 对风险表现出良好判断的

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie cautious to caution, to the -ous ending and to the picture of testing the ground.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把 cautious 与 caution、-ous 词尾以及试探地面的画面连起来。

normal.en: Cautious is caution plus -ous, just as dangerous is danger plus -ous.
normal.cn: cautious 就是 caution 加 -ous，正如 dangerous 是 danger 加 -ous。

normal.en: The Latin root cavere, to beware, also hides in caveat, a warning.
normal.cn: 拉丁语词根 cavere（当心）也藏在 caveat（警告）里。

normal.en: Cautious optimism means hoping for the best while watching for the worst.
normal.cn: cautious optimism 意为盼最好的结果，同时防最坏的情况。

normal.en: Cautious about is the usual pairing before a risk: cautious about money, about strangers.
normal.cn: cautious about 是风险前的常见搭配，如对钱、对陌生人谨慎。

normal.en: More cautious and most cautious use helpers because the adjective is long.
normal.cn: 比较级和最高级用 more 与 most，因为词形较长。

abstract.en: Picture a foot testing thin ice before the weight shifts.
abstract.cn: 想象一只脚在重心移动前先试探薄冰。

abstract.en: Picture a driver leaving a wide gap on a wet road.
abstract.cn: 想象司机在湿滑路面上留出很宽的车距。

abstract.en: Picture a speaker pausing before answering a dangerous question.
abstract.cn: 想象发言者在回答棘手问题前停顿了一下。

examples.en: She is cautious about lending money.
examples.cn: 她借钱给别人很谨慎。

examples.en: The doctor was cautious but hopeful.
examples.cn: 医生态度谨慎但抱有希望。

examples.en: They took a cautious step onto the bridge.
examples.cn: 他们小心地踏上桥面。

dict_mnemonic.text: cautious 里有 caution：心里常存一句「当心」，走路说话就会变得谨慎。

root: 由英语 caution 加 -ous 构成，caution 源自拉丁语 cautio，出自动词 cavere（当心、提防）。

sensesIntro.en: Watching your step gives the everyday sense, and watching your words gives the guarded sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 看住脚下给出日常义，看住口中的话给出有保留义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot testing the ground before the weight goes down.
core.cn: 核心意象：重心落下前先用脚试探地面。

branches.en: Physical care keeps the word close to danger and harm.
branches.cn: 身体上的小心让这个词贴近危险与伤害。

branches.en: Guarded speech applies the same watchfulness to promises.
branches.cn: 有保留的言语把同样的警觉用到承诺上。

branches.en: Cautious about money and strangers keeps the risk sense concrete.
branches.cn: 对钱和陌生人的谨慎让风险义保持具体。

branches.en: Both senses avoid committing too fast.
branches.cn: 两个义项都避免过快作出承诺。

branches.en: Cautious optimism shows the word at its most public and political.
branches.cn: 谨慎乐观展示了这个词最公开、最政治化的一面。

intro.en: Cautious shares the caution family and takes -ly and -ness for its adverb and noun.
intro.cn: cautious 与 caution 同族，并用 -ly、-ness 构成副词与名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb cavere, to beware, also gives caveat and incautious.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 cavere（当心）也给出 caveat 与 incautious。

items.exampleCN: 他的谨慎挽救了这笔交易。

items.example: One incautious word cost him the job.
items.exampleCN: 一句不慎的话让他丢了工作。

items.example: Cautio is the source of caution.
items.exampleCN: cautio 是 caution 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Cautio passed into French as caution.
latinEntries.exampleCN: cautio 传入法语成为 caution。

latinEntries.example: Cavere is the deep root of cautious.
latinEntries.exampleCN: cavere 是 cautious 的深层词根。

definition_zh: 难民；避难者
definition_en: a person who has been forced to leave their country because of war, persecution, or disaster
core_image: 边境营地里排着长队等待热汤的人群
scene: 边境的临时营地里，人们排着长队领取热汤，队伍一直延伸到帐篷后面。 Thousands of refugees crossed the border that winter.
sceneCN: 这里 refugees 是 refugee 的复数，取「难民」（第 1 个义项：因战争或迫害被迫离乡的人）；句意为那个冬天成千上万的难民越过了边境。画面里可留意：长队、热汤、帐篷后的队伍。

derivatives.zh: 避难所；庇护
难民处境

senses.title: One who flees for safety
senses.definition: a person forced to leave home and country by war, persecution, or disaster
senses.definitionCN: 因战争、迫害或灾难被迫离开家园与祖国的人
senses.example: Thousands of refugees crossed the border that winter.
senses.exampleCN: 那个冬天成千上万的难民越过了边境。
senses.why: The Latin root is to flee, and the ending marks the person who has done the fleeing and is now seeking shelter.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「逃」，词尾标记的正是那个已经逃出、正在寻求庇护的人。

senses.title: One seeking shelter
senses.definition: a person who has left a dangerous place and is looking for protection elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 离开危险之地、在别处寻求保护的人
senses.example: The church gave shelter to refugees from the flooded valley.
senses.exampleCN: 教堂收留了来自被洪水淹没的山谷的避难者。
senses.why: The word can be used more loosely for anyone in flight, not only for those with legal refugee status.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也可较宽泛地指任何在逃亡中的人，而不只是拥有法定难民身份的人。

intro.en: Refugee names the person at the end of a flight: the Latin verb is to flee, and the noun is the one who has fled and asks for shelter.
intro.cn: refugee 指逃亡终点的那个人：拉丁动词意为「逃」，名词则指已经逃出并请求庇护的人。

items.en: Fugere meant to flee or run away, the base of the family.
items.cn: fugere 意为逃跑或逃走，是这个词族的词根。

items.en: Refugium joined re-, back, with fugere and named a place to which one flees back for safety.
items.cn: refugium 由 re-（往回）与 fugere 组成，指逃回去寻求安全的地方。

items.en: French réfugié named the Protestants who left France in the seventeenth century for their faith.
items.cn: 法语 réfugié 指十七世纪因信仰离开法国的新教徒。

items.en: English borrowed the word and widened it from a religious exile to any person driven out by war or disaster.
items.cn: 英语借入这个词，并从宗教流亡者扩展到任何因战争或灾难被逐出的人。

items.en: International law in the twentieth century fixed refugee as a legal status with defined rights.
items.cn: 二十世纪的国际法把 refugee 固定为一种带有明确权利的法律身份。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the same opening syllables; the near-meaning group gathers names for people in flight or in need of protection.
note.cn: 形近组收开头音节相近的词；近义组收表示逃亡者或需受保护者的名称。

entries.definition: A place of safety.
An official who judges a game.
To say no to something.
One who runs from the law or danger.
One asking a country for protection.
One living away from home by force.
One forced from their home by war.

normalIntro.en: The word ends in ee, the ending for a person, and the stem is to flee: a refugee is the one who fled.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词以 ee 结尾，这是表示「人」的词尾，词干意为「逃」：refugee 就是那个逃出来的人。

normal.en: Fugere is to flee, and a refugee is the person who did it.
normal.cn: fugere 是逃跑，refugee 就是逃的那个人。

normal.en: A refuge is the shelter; a refugee is the one who needs it.
normal.cn: refuge 是避难所，refugee 是需要它的人。

normal.en: A refugee camp is a camp for those who have fled.
normal.cn: refugee camp 是为逃难者设的营地。

normal.en: Political refugees leave because of their beliefs.
normal.cn: political refugees 因信念而离开。

normal.en: Refugee and refuge differ only by the ending of the person.
normal.cn: refugee 与 refuge 的差别只在于那个指人的词尾。

abstract.en: A refugee is a person whose address was taken away.
abstract.cn: 难民，是地址被人夺走的人。

abstract.en: The word asks the reader to remember the road, not only the camp.
abstract.cn: 这个词要人记住那条路，而不只是那个营地。

abstract.en: Shelter is a right, and a refugee is the test of that right.
abstract.cn: 庇护是一项权利，而难民正是这项权利的试金石。

examples.en: Thousands of refugees crossed the border that winter.
examples.cn: 那个冬天成千上万的难民越过了边境。

examples.en: The church gave shelter to refugees from the flooded valley.
examples.cn: 教堂收留了来自被洪水淹没的山谷的避难者。

examples.en: He arrived as a refugee with one bag and no papers.
examples.cn: 他作为一个难民来到这里，只带一个包，没有证件。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（往回、寻庇护）加 fug（逃）加 ee（人）：逃出去寻找庇护的人，就是难民。

root: 拉丁 fugere（逃）→ refugium（避难之地）→ 法语 réfugié（流亡者）→ 英语 refugee；同族有 refuge，形近的 fugitive 也出自 fugere。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a person who fled; the senses move from the legal refugee to anyone seeking shelter.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「已经逃出的人」；义项从法律意义上的难民，扩展到任何寻求庇护的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long line for hot soup in a border camp, running past the tents.
core.cn: 核心意象：边境营地里排到帐篷后面的领汤长队。

branches.en: a family crossing at night
branches.cn: 夜里越过边境的一家人

branches.en: a church opening its doors
branches.cn: 敞开大门的教堂

branches.en: the one who fled and the one who shelters
branches.cn: 逃出的人与收留他的人

branches.en: a bag with no papers
branches.cn: 一个没有证件的包

branches.en: a queue that reaches the tents
branches.cn: 一直排到帐篷前的队伍

intro.en: A Latin verb of fleeing takes a prefix of return and a noun ending, and then a person-ending names the one who fled.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的「逃」动词接上表返回的前缀与名词词尾，再由指人的词尾命名那个逃出的人。

latinIntro.en: The base is fugere, to flee; re- means back, and -ium makes a place, while -ee names the person.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 fugere（逃）；re- 表「往回」，-ium 构成表地点的名词，-ee 则指人。

definition_zh: 立方体；立方；切成小方块
definition_en: a solid shape with six equal square faces, or to cut food into blocks
core_image: 一颗骰子停在桌面上，每个面都是正方形
scene: 骰子停在桌角，朝上一面正好是正方形。 Cut the bread into small cubes before drying it.
sceneCN: 这里 cube 指「立方体」（第 1 个义项：六个面都是正方形的立体）；句意是先把面包切成小方块再烘干。

derivatives.zh: 立方体的；立方的
立方形的
长方体

senses.title: A six-sided solid
senses.definition: a solid with six equal square faces
senses.definitionCN: 六个相等的正方形面构成的立体
senses.example: The box is a perfect cube.
senses.exampleCN: 这个盒子是一个完整的立方体。
senses.why: Every face agrees with the other five.
senses.whyCN: 每个面都和另外五个面一样。

senses.title: A third power
senses.definition: the number you get by multiplying a number by itself twice
senses.definitionCN: 把一个数自乘两次所得的数
senses.example: The cube of three is twenty-seven.
senses.exampleCN: 三的立方是二十七。
senses.why: Three equal lengths fill one solid space.
senses.whyCN: 三段相等的长度填满一个立体。

senses.title: Cut into blocks
senses.definition: to cut something into small cube shapes
senses.definitionCN: 把某物切成小方块
senses.example: Cube the potatoes before frying them.
senses.exampleCN: 炸之前把土豆切成小方块。
senses.why: A knife turns soft food into geometry.
senses.whyCN: 刀把软的食物切成几何形。

intro.en: Cube comes from Greek kybos, a die, through Latin cubus and French cube.
intro.cn: cube 源自希腊语 kybos（骰子），经拉丁语 cubus 与法语 cube 进入英语。

items.en: Kybos meant a cube or a dice.
items.cn: kybos 指立方体或骰子。

items.en: It also described a piled heap of grain.
items.cn: 它也能形容堆起的谷堆。

items.en: Cubus kept the shape of the six-faced solid.
items.cn: cubus 保留了六面立体的形状。

items.en: Cube named the solid with equal square faces.
items.cn: cube 指各面为相等正方形的立体。

items.en: Cube entered English and later named a third power.
items.cn: cube 进入英语，后来也指三次方。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cu- opening, and the meaning group names other solid blocks.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cu- 开头，近义组列出其他实心块状物的说法。

entries.definition: a young wild animal
the raised edge of a road
pleasing to look at
a solid piece with flat sides
a small cube used in games
a shape with length, width, and height

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a die on a table and end with potatoes under a knife.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从桌上一颗骰子开始，落到刀下的土豆。

normal.en: Six squares, all the same, make one cube.
normal.cn: 六个一样的正方形，做成一个立方体。

normal.en: A die is just a cube that learned to roll.
normal.cn: 骰子就是一个学会打滚的立方体。

normal.en: Multiply a number by itself twice and you cube it.
normal.cn: 把一个数自乘两次，就是求它的立方。

normal.en: Soup tastes better when the vegetables are cubed.
normal.cn: 蔬菜切成小块，汤就更好喝。

normal.en: A cube has no front and no back, only faces.
normal.cn: 立方体没有前后，只有一个个面。

abstract.en: Picture a sugar lump melting in a hot cup.
abstract.cn: 想象一块方糖在热杯里化开。

abstract.en: Picture three equal sticks filling one box.
abstract.cn: 想象三根等长的棍子填满一个盒子。

abstract.en: Picture a tray of potatoes cut into squares.
abstract.cn: 想象一盘切成方块的土豆。

examples.en: The ice in the glass is one large cube.
examples.cn: 杯里的冰是一大块立方体。

examples.en: Cube the cheese and add it to the salad.
examples.cn: 把奶酪切成小块加进沙拉。

examples.en: The cube of four is sixty-four.
examples.cn: 四的立方是六十四。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cube 记成「骰子」：希腊语 kybos 就是骰子，六个面一样大。

root: 源自希腊语 kybos（骰子、立方体），经拉丁语 cubus 与法语 cube 进入英语；本义是六面相等的骰子形，后指数学上的立方与切成方块。

sensesIntro.en: From a six-sided solid, to a third power, to food cut into blocks.
sensesIntro.cn: 从六面的立体，到三次方，再到切成方块的食物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a die resting on a table, every face a square.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗骰子停在桌上，每个面都是正方形。

branches.en: Six equal squares fold into one solid.
branches.cn: 六个相等的正方形围成一个立体。

branches.en: Two multiplications turn a length into a volume.
branches.cn: 两次相乘，把长度变成体积。

branches.en: A knife repeats the same shape in food.
branches.cn: 刀在食物上重复同一种形状。

branches.en: The shape and the power carry one name.
branches.cn: 形状和乘方共用一个名字。

branches.en: A whole cube and a small piece of it look alike.
branches.cn: 整块立方体与它的小块长得很像。

intro.en: Cube forms a small family for shape, power, and cutting things into blocks.
intro.cn: cube 组成一小族词，关于形状、乘方与切成方块。

latinIntro.en: The Greek kybos, a die, is the root behind cube and cubic.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 kybos（骰子）是 cube 与 cubic 背后的根。

items.exampleCN: 每个立方体有十二条棱。

items.example: The room is ten cubic metres.
A cubical box sat on the floor.
items.exampleCN: 地板上放着一只方形箱子。

items.meaning: the number that gives a cube
items.example: The cube root of eight is two.
He dropped a sugar cube in the tea.
items.exampleCN: 他往茶里放了一块方糖。

items.meaning: a small block of ice for drinks
items.example: Add two ice cubes to the glass.

items.meaning: an art style built from simple shapes
items.meaningCN: 以简单几何形构成的艺术风格
items.example: Cubism broke faces into flat shapes.
items.exampleCN: 立体主义把人脸拆成平面形状。

definition_zh: 腐烂的；变质的；糟糕的；腐败的
definition_en: decayed and soft, very bad, or morally corrupt
core_image: 一只长满霉斑的苹果
scene: 厨房里传来腐烂水果的臭味。 A rotten smell came from the fruit in the kitchen.
sceneCN: 这里 rotten 是「腐烂的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：厨房里传来腐烂水果的臭味。

derivatives.zh: 腐烂；腐败
腐烂；腐败
腐烂的过程

senses.title: Decayed
senses.definition: soft and bad because of decay
senses.definitionCN: 因腐烂而变软变坏
senses.example: The basket was full of rotten apples.
senses.exampleCN: 篮子里装满了烂苹果。
senses.why: The fruit has broken down and cannot be eaten.
senses.whyCN: 水果已经分解变质，不能吃了。

senses.title: Very bad
senses.definition: very unpleasant or of very poor quality
senses.definitionCN: 非常令人不快或质量极差
senses.example: We had rotten weather all week.
senses.exampleCN: 我们一整周都碰上糟糕的天气。
senses.why: The idea of decay spreads to bad conditions.
senses.whyCN: 腐烂的概念扩展到恶劣的状况。

senses.title: Corrupt
senses.definition: dishonest and morally bad
senses.definitionCN: 不诚实且在道德上败坏的
senses.example: The film shows a rotten system at work.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影展现了一个腐败体制的运作。
senses.why: A society can decay like fruit.
senses.whyCN: 社会也会像水果一样腐烂。

intro.en: Rotten comes from Old Norse rotinn, decayed.
intro.cn: rotten 源自古代诺斯语 rotinn，意为腐烂的。

items.en: Rotinn means decayed or putrid.
items.cn: rotinn 意为腐烂的、发臭的。

items.en: Rotna means to rot away.
items.cn: rotna 意为逐渐腐烂。

items.en: Rotian means to decay.
items.cn: rotian 意为腐坏。

items.en: Rotten keeps the sense of spoiled food.
items.cn: rotten 保留食物变坏的含义。

items.en: Rotten also means very bad or corrupt.
items.cn: rotten 又表示糟糕或腐败。

note.en: Rotten food has decayed; bad food may just taste poor.
note.cn: rotten 指已经腐烂，bad 只表示不好。

entries.definition: to decay slowly
decaying
the state of being rotten
damaged by rot
no longer good to eat
of poor quality

normalIntro.en: Rotten fruit has gone soft, dark, and smelly.
normalIntro.cn: rotten 的水果已经变软、发黑、发臭。

normal.en: Throw out the rotten eggs at once.
normal.cn: 立刻把臭鸡蛋扔掉。

normal.en: A rotten smell filled the cellar.
normal.cn: 地窖里弥漫着腐烂的气味。

normal.en: It was rotten luck to miss the train.
normal.cn: 错过火车真是倒霉。

normal.en: One rotten apple can spoil the basket.
normal.cn: 一个烂苹果能坏掉一整篮。

normal.en: The fruit went rotten in the heat.
normal.cn: 水果在高温下腐烂了。

abstract.en: Picture an apple covered in dark spots.
abstract.cn: 想象一只布满黑斑的苹果。

abstract.en: Imagine a wooden beam soft with damp.
abstract.cn: 想象一根被潮气泡软的木梁。

abstract.en: Think of a system hollowed out from within.
abstract.cn: 想象一个从内部被掏空的体制。

examples.en: The air was heavy with the smell of rotten wood.
examples.cn: 空气里满是朽木的气味。

examples.en: We lost the match through rotten luck.
examples.cn: 我们因倒霉输掉了比赛。

examples.en: The report exposed a rotten deal.
examples.cn: 报告揭露了一桩腐败交易。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rot（烂）＋ ten」——烂到发软发臭，就是腐烂的；事情烂到根上，就是糟糕、腐败的。

root: 古代诺斯语 rotinn（腐烂的）与 rotna（腐烂）→ rotten，核心义「已经分解败坏」。

sensesIntro.en: Rotten means decayed, very bad, or morally corrupt.
sensesIntro.cn: rotten 意为腐烂变质的、非常糟糕的，或道德腐败的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an apple covered in mold.
core.cn: 核心意象：长满霉斑的苹果。

branches.en: Decayed food is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 腐烂食物是字面义项。

branches.en: Bad conditions borrow the decay image.
branches.cn: 恶劣状况借用腐烂意象。

branches.en: Corruption is moral rot.
branches.cn: 腐败就是道德上的腐烂。

branches.en: Both describe something spoiled.
branches.cn: 两者都形容被败坏之物。

branches.en: Physical and moral decay share one root.
branches.cn: 物质与道德腐败共享同一根源。

intro.en: Rotten comes from a Germanic verb meaning to decay.
intro.cn: rotten 来自表示腐烂的日耳曼语动词。

latinIntro.en: Rotten has no Latin root; it is Norse and English.
latinIntro.cn: rotten 没有拉丁词根，它来自诺斯语与英语。

definition_zh: 无尽的；没完没了的
definition_en: having no end, or seeming to continue for too long
core_image: 沙漠一直延伸到天边，看不到终点
scene: 沙漠在热浪里显得无边无际。 The desert looked endless in the heat.
sceneCN: 这里 endless 是「无边无际的」（第 1 个义项：似乎没有尽头）；句意：沙漠在热浪里显得无边无际。

derivatives.zh: 无尽地；不断地
无尽；冗长

senses.title: Having no visible end
senses.definition: seeming to have no limit in space or time
senses.definitionCN: 在空间或时间上似乎没有边界
senses.example: The desert looked endless in the heat.
senses.exampleCN: 沙漠在热浪里显得无边无际。
senses.why: The suffix -less removes the end, so the word pictures something stretching beyond sight.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -less 去掉了尽头，因此这个词描绘延伸到视野之外的事物。

senses.title: Tiringly long
senses.definition: continuing so long that it feels boring or exhausting
senses.definitionCN: 持续太久以致令人厌烦或疲惫
senses.example: The meeting felt endless.
senses.exampleCN: 会议感觉没完没了。
senses.why: What has no end in sight can wear a person down, so the word also carries impatience.
senses.whyCN: 看不到终点的事物会消耗人，因此这个词也带不耐烦的意味。

intro.en: Endless is end plus the old suffix -less, meaning without.
intro.cn: endless 是 end 加古老词尾 -less，意为没有。

items.en: Endeleas already means without end.
items.cn: 古英语 endelēas 已意为没有尽头。

items.en: The spelling settles as endless.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 endless。

items.en: Endless describes long roads, waits, and speeches.
items.cn: 在近代早期，endless 描述漫长的道路、等待与讲话。

items.en: The word gains the sense of tediously long.
items.cn: 这个词获得冗长烦人的含义。

items.en: Endless often appears in phrases about possibilities and delays.
items.cn: 当代英语中，endless 常用于可能性和拖延的表述。

note.en: Endless means no end in sight; infinite is more exact, and nonstop means without pause.
note.cn: endless 指看不到尽头，infinite 更精确，nonstop 指不停顿。

entries.definition: the last point
the final part
without stopping
without any limit
having no boundaries
continuing without a pause

normalIntro.en: Endless is end plus -less: an end taken away, so the road runs on.
normalIntro.cn: endless 是 end 加 -less：去掉了尽头，所以路一直延伸。

normal.en: The desert seemed endless.
normal.cn: 沙漠似乎无边无际。

normal.en: The wait felt endless.
normal.cn: 等待感觉没完没了。

normal.en: Endless possibilities lie ahead.
normal.cn: 前方有无限可能。

normal.en: The -less ending means without.
normal.cn: 词尾 -less 意为没有。

normal.en: Endlessly means without stopping.
normal.cn: endlessly 意为不停。

abstract.en: Picture a road meeting a flat horizon.
abstract.cn: 想象道路与平坦地平线相接。

abstract.en: See a queue that never moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一条始终不动的队伍。

abstract.en: Think of waves repeating on a dark sea.
abstract.cn: 想象暗色海面上重复的波浪。

examples.en: The desert looked endless in the heat.
examples.cn: 沙漠在热浪里显得无边无际。

examples.en: The meeting felt endless.
examples.cn: 会议感觉没完没了。

examples.en: Endless possibilities lie ahead.
examples.cn: 前方有无限可能。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安得勒斯」——走到「安」静尽头却还是路；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 endelēas，由 end（尽头）加 -less（没有）构成。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers space or time without a visible limit, and duration that wears patience thin.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词涵盖看不到边界的空间或时间，以及消磨耐心的漫长持续。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road running beyond the horizon.
core.cn: 核心意象：延伸到地平线之外的道路。

branches.en: The base sense is having no visible limit.
branches.cn: 基本义是看不到界限。

branches.en: Too much length in time becomes weariness.
branches.cn: 时间上的过长变成疲惫。

branches.en: A space without end and a wait without end share one shape.
branches.cn: 无边的空间与无尽的等待共享同一种形状。

branches.en: The -less suffix removes the boundary.
branches.cn: 词尾 -less 移除了边界。

branches.en: Endless tasks make people sigh.
branches.cn: 没完没了的任务让人叹气。

intro.en: Endless is end plus -less, the suffix for lacking something.
intro.cn: endless 是 end 加 -less，即表示缺乏某物的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Endless is purely Germanic; Latin-based synonyms include infinite.
latinIntro.cn: endless 纯属日耳曼来源，拉丁来源的近义词是 infinite。

items.example: End is the base of endless.
items.exampleCN: end 是 endless 的基础。
infinite 是拉丁来源的近义词。

definition_zh: 更好的；上级的
definition_en: better than another, or higher in rank
core_image: 两座塔并排，其中一座明显更高
scene: 这种材料在耐用性上优于那种。 This material is superior to that one in durability.
sceneCN: 这里 superior 是「更好的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这种材料在耐用性上优于那种。

derivatives.zh: 优越性
在上方

senses.title: Better in quality
senses.definition: higher in quality than another
senses.definitionCN: 质量上高于另一者
senses.example: This material is superior to that one in durability.
senses.exampleCN: 这种材料在耐用性上优于那种。
senses.why: This is the comparative quality sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是比较质量的义项。

senses.title: Higher in rank
senses.definition: having a higher position
senses.definitionCN: 职位更高
senses.example: Report the problem to your superior officer.
senses.exampleCN: 把问题报告给你的上级军官。

definition_zh: 登上；骑上；增加；安装；山
definition_en: to climb onto something such as a horse or a platform; to increase gradually; to fix something in position for use or display; a mountain, especially in names
core_image: 一个人抓着缰绳翻身上马，脚下石阶一级级往高处去
scene: 清晨的山道上，老人抓住缰绳，一脚踩稳马镫，翻身坐上马背。 He mounted the grey horse and rode slowly up the stone path.
sceneCN: 这里「mount」是「登上、骑上」（第 1 个义项：爬上某物或骑上马背）；句意为他骑上那匹灰马，顺着石阶慢慢往山上走。画面里能想见：山道、缰绳、马镫与马背。

collocations.zh: 发起一场运动；开展一场活动

derivatives.zh: 由否定前缀 dis- 加 mount 构成，义为「下马；下车」
由前缀 re- 加 mount 构成，义为「重新骑上；重新安装」
由 mount 加 -ing 构成，义为「底座；装架；装裱材料」
由 mount 加 -able 构成，义为「可安装的；可骑上的」

senses.title: To climb onto a horse, bicycle or raised surface
senses.definition: to get onto a horse or bicycle, or to climb up onto a platform, wall or high place
senses.definitionCN: 上马或上车，或爬上一个台子、墙头或高处
senses.example: He mounted the grey horse and rode slowly up the stone path.
senses.exampleCN: 他骑上那匹灰马，顺着石阶慢慢往山上走。
senses.why: Mount comes from Latin mons, a mountain, through a verb that meant to go up; the first sense is simply upward movement onto something.
senses.whyCN: mount 经一个表示「往上走」的动词，来自拉丁语 mons（山）；第一个义项就是往上升、上到某物之上。

senses.title: To increase gradually, often until it becomes serious
senses.definition: to grow in amount, strength or intensity over time, especially in a way that causes concern
senses.definitionCN: 数量、力量或强度随时间增长，尤指增长到令人担忧的程度
senses.example: Pressure mounted on the committee as the deadline approached.
senses.exampleCN: 随着截止日期临近，委员会承受的压力越来越大。
senses.why: Going up is the core motion of the word, and a number or a feeling that goes up behaves like a climber gaining height.
senses.whyCN: 「往上走」是这个词的核心动作，而不断上升的数字或情绪，就像越爬越高的攀登者。

senses.title: To fix something in position for use or display
senses.definition: to attach an object firmly to a frame, wall or base so that it can be used, shown or studied
senses.definitionCN: 把某物牢固地装到框架、墙面或底座上，以便使用、展示或研究
senses.example: The technician mounted the camera above the entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 技术员把相机安装在入口上方。
senses.why: A thing placed up on a support is literally mounted, so the word keeps the upward picture while shifting from climbing to fixing in place.
senses.whyCN: 一件被放到支架上方的东西，字面上就是被 mount 上去，所以这个词从「爬上去」转为「固定住」时，仍保留着向上放置的画面。

senses.title: A mountain, especially in names and literary writing
senses.definition: a mountain or high hill, used mainly in proper names such as Mount Tai and in older or literary style
senses.definitionCN: 山或高山，主要用于泰山这类专名，以及较旧或文学性的文体中
senses.example: Snow still covered the upper slopes of the mount in early spring.
senses.exampleCN: 早春时，这座山的上部山坡仍覆着雪。
senses.why: The noun is the oldest layer of the word: Latin mons meant a mountain, and the name of the height stayed in English long after the verb took over everyday use.
senses.whyCN: 名词是这个词最古老的一层：拉丁语 mons 本义就是山，这一「高处之名」在动词接管日常用法之后很久仍留在英语里。

intro.en: Mount goes back to a Latin word for mountain, which also produced a verb meaning to climb; French carried both the height and the upward movement into English.
intro.cn: mount 可追到拉丁语表示「山」的词，同一个词又造出意为「攀登」的动词；法语把「高处」与「向上移动」这两层都带进了英语。

items.en: Mons meant a mountain or a high hill, and its stem mont- appears in mountain, amount and many place names.
items.cn: mons 意为山或高丘，其词干 mont- 出现在 mountain、amount 和许多地名中。

items.en: Everyday Latin built a verb montare from mons, meaning to go up or to climb; it is not recorded in formal texts but survives in the Romance languages.
items.cn: 民间拉丁语从 mons 造出动词 montare，意为往上走、攀登；它在正式文献中没有记录，却留在罗曼语族里。

items.en: Old French monter carried the senses of climbing, rising and getting on a horse, and it passed into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 monter 兼有攀登、上升与上马的意思，诺曼时期之后传入英语。

items.en: Middle English mounten covered climbing a hill, getting on horseback and rising in rank or value.
items.cn: 中古英语 mounten 涵盖爬山、上马，以及地位或价值的上升。

items.en: Modern English keeps the upward senses, adds fixing an object on a support, organizing a campaign, and the noun for a mountain used in names.
items.cn: 现代英语保留上升类义项，又添上把物件固定到支架上、组织一场运动，以及用于山名的名词义。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin mountain stem and its English family; the near-meaning group gathers words for climbing, rising and fixing in place.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语「山」词干及其英语词族展开；近义组收表示攀登、上升与固定安装的词。

entries.definition: A total or quantity, from the same Latin verb for going up.
entries.definitionCN: 总额或数量，来自同一个表示「往上升」的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: To get down off a horse or bicycle.
To overcome a difficulty, or to stand on top of something.
entries.definitionCN: 克服困难，或位于某物之上。

entries.definition: A very high hill, built on the Latin mountain word.
entries.definitionCN: 很高的山，建立在拉丁语「山」这个词上。

entries.definition: A picture or film assembled from several pieces, from a French word for mounting.
entries.definitionCN: 把若干片段拼起来的画面或影片，源自法语中表示「装配」的词。

entries.definition: To go up something using hands and feet, or to rise steadily.
entries.definitionCN: 手脚并用地爬上某物，或稳定上升。

entries.definition: To move upwards, often in a steady or ceremonial way.
entries.definitionCN: 向上移动，常指平稳或庄重的上升。

entries.definition: To become larger in amount or degree.
To fix equipment in place so that it can be used.
entries.definitionCN: 把设备安装到位以便使用。

normalIntro.en: The word climbs out of a Latin mountain word, and its family keeps returning to height, upward movement and things placed on a support.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从拉丁语表示「山」的词里爬出来，词族反复回到高度、向上的运动，以及被放到支架上的东西。

normal.en: Mons is Latin for mountain, so mount begins as a word about height and going up.
normal.cn: mons 是拉丁语的「山」，所以 mount 起初是一个关于高处与往上走的词。

normal.en: Old French monter gave English the verb, which is why mount and mountain look like relatives.
normal.cn: 古法语 monter 给了英语这个动词，所以 mount 与 mountain 看起来像亲戚。

normal.en: Dismount adds dis-: the reverse of getting on, therefore getting off.
normal.cn: dismount 加 dis-：与「上去」相反，因此是「下来」。

normal.en: Surmount adds sur- (above): to rise over an obstacle.
normal.cn: surmount 加 sur-（在上方）：升到障碍之上，即克服。

normal.en: 「Mounting costs」 are costs that keep climbing, and a picture mount is a support that holds the picture up.
normal.cn: 不断上升的成本像在往上爬，而画作的底座是把画托起来的东西。

abstract.en: Every sense of mount is a version of upward movement: a rider rises onto a horse, a number rises, a picture is lifted onto a wall.
abstract.cn: mount 的每个义项都是「向上」的一种版本：骑手升上马背，数字升高，画作被托上墙面。

abstract.en: A mountain is the most permanent thing one can mount, which is why the noun for height outlived the everyday verb.
abstract.cn: 山是人能登上的最持久的东西，所以表示高度的名词比日常动词活得更久。

abstract.en: Mounting a campaign is climbing in another form: gathering force until the effort stands above the noise.
abstract.cn: 发起一场运动是另一种形式的攀登：积蓄力量，直到这份努力高过周围的噪音。

examples.en: He mounted the grey horse and rode slowly up the stone path.
examples.cn: 他骑上那匹灰马，顺着石阶慢慢往山上走。

examples.en: Pressure mounted on the committee as the deadline approached.
examples.cn: 随着截止日期临近，委员会承受的压力越来越大。

examples.en: The technician mounted the camera above the entrance.
examples.cn: 技术员把相机安装在入口上方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「芒特」——登山的人喘着气喊出这个名字；mount 就是登上、攀升，也指山。

root: 拉丁语 mons（山，词干 mont-）在民间拉丁语中造出 montare（往上走、攀登），经古法语 monter 进入英语；同族词多与上升、山、安装有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is upward movement from and toward a height; the senses read it as climbing onto something, rising in degree, being placed on a support, and the height itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是朝高处、从高处发生的向上运动；义项把它读成爬上某物、程度上升、被放到支架上，以及高处本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rider gripping the reins and swinging up onto a horse, with stone steps climbing ahead.
core.cn: 核心意象：骑手抓住缰绳翻身上马，前面的石阶一级级往上。

branches.en: a rider lifting a boot into the stirrup
branches.cn: 骑手把靴子踏进马镫

branches.en: a pressure gauge needle creeping upward
branches.cn: 压力表指针一点点上移

branches.en: a camera raised and fixed above a door
branches.cn: 相机被举高并固定在门上方

branches.en: a picture lifted onto a gallery wall
branches.cn: 画作被托上画廊的墙

branches.en: a snow line drawn across a high ridge
branches.cn: 高脊上画出的雪线

intro.en: A Latin mountain word and its everyday verb, a French climbing verb and four English formations carry mount from a height to a motion, a support and a campaign.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语「山」词及其民间动词、一个法语攀登动词，加上四个英语构词形式，把 mount 从高处带到运动、支架与一场运动。

latinIntro.en: Mons, its accusative montem and the everyday verb montare are Latin forms behind the English family; montare appears only in informal usage.
latinIntro.cn: mons、它的宾格 montem 与民间动词 montare 是英语这一族词背后的拉丁词形；montare 只见于非正式用法。

senses.title: To stick fast to a surface
senses.definition: to stick or hold firmly to a surface, often by natural or chemical means
senses.definitionCN: 紧紧贴住或附着在某个表面上，多靠自然力或化学作用
senses.example: The label adheres best to a dry, clean surface.
senses.exampleCN: 这种标签在干燥洁净的表面上黏得最牢。
senses.why: The Latin verb haerere means to stick or stay fixed, and ad- adds direction towards something, so the word pictures contact that will not let go.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 haerere 意为「粘住、固定不动」，ad- 又加上「朝向」的方向，所以这个词画出的是一种不肯松开的接触。

senses.title: To follow a rule or promise
senses.definition: to act in accordance with a rule, agreement or standard
senses.definitionCN: 按照规则、约定或标准行事
senses.example: All staff must adhere to the safety rules.
senses.exampleCN: 全体员工都必须遵守安全规定。
senses.why: A rule that you adhere to is one you stay stuck to; the physical image of clinging is transferred to conduct.
senses.whyCN: 你 adhere to 的规则，是你「贴住不放」的规则；身体上的黏附被移用到行为上。

senses.title: To stay loyal to a leader or group
senses.definition: to give continued support to a person, party or cause
senses.definitionCN: 持续支持某个人、政党或事业
senses.example: Several senators refused to adhere to the new party line.
senses.exampleCN: 几位参议员拒绝追随新的党派路线。
senses.why: Here people are the surfaces: supporters stay attached to a leader instead of drifting away.
senses.whyCN: 这里的人是「表面」：拥护者紧贴着领袖，而不是飘走。

intro.en: One Latin verb of sticking supplies both the physical and the moral senses.
intro.cn: 一个表示「粘住」的拉丁动词，同时供给了物理义与道义义。

items.en: haerere meant to stick, cling or stay fixed, and also to be stuck in doubt.
items.cn: haerere 意为粘住、紧贴、固定不动，也有「困在疑惑中」的意思。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus haerere formed adhaerere, to stick to, with the noun adhaesio for the act of sticking.
items.cn: ad-（向）加 haerere 构成 adhaerere「黏附于」，名词 adhaesio 表示黏附这一动作。

items.en: Old French adherer carried the physical and the figurative senses side by side.
items.cn: 古法语 adherer 把物理义与比喻义一并带了过来。

items.en: English took the verb in the fifteenth century, first for physical sticking, soon for holding to opinions.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个动词，先指物理上的黏附，很快也指坚持某种意见。

items.en: Technical writing keeps the literal sense, while law and politics use it for obedience and loyalty.
items.cn: 技术文献保留字面义，法律与政治则用它表示遵守与忠诚。

note.en: The first group is the haerere family; the second gathers verbs of sticking and of compliance.
note.cn: 第一组是 haerere 词族；第二组收黏住与服从两路动词。

entries.definition: the act of following a rule or belief
a supporter of a party or idea
the physical force of sticking
a substance that sticks things together
to fix itself to a surface
to hold on tightly
to obey a rule or request
to accept or remain faithful to

normalIntro.en: The core is haerere, Latin for to stick.
normalIntro.cn: 核心是拉丁语 haerere，意为「粘住」。

normal.en: ad- plus haerere gives adhere, to stick onto something.
normal.cn: ad- 加 haerere 就是 adhere，贴到某物上。

normal.en: adhere to works for surfaces and for rules alike.
normal.cn: adhere to 既能接表面，也能接规则。

normal.en: adhesion names the sticking, adherence names the keeping of a rule.
normal.cn: adhesion 指「黏附」，adherence 指「遵守」。

normal.en: adhesive keeps the adjective ending and is used as a noun for glue.
normal.cn: adhesive 保留了形容词词尾，却常作名词指胶粘剂。

normal.en: Formal writing prefers strictly adhere to.
normal.cn: 正式文体偏爱 strictly adhere to（严格遵守）。

abstract.en: See a stamp pressed onto an envelope and refusing to peel off.
abstract.cn: 想象一张邮票压上信封，怎么揭都揭不下来。

abstract.en: Picture a climber's hand locked on a hold.
abstract.cn: 想象攀岩者的手死死扣住岩点。

abstract.en: Think of a member who never misses the party line.
abstract.cn: 想象一名从不偏离党派路线的成员。

examples.en: The label adheres best to a dry, clean surface.
examples.cn: 这种标签在干燥洁净的表面上黏得最牢。

examples.en: Members must adhere to the club's rules.
examples.cn: 会员必须遵守俱乐部的规定。

examples.en: He adheres to the old belief that hard work solves most problems.
examples.cn: 他信奉那个老观念：努力能解决大部分问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额的赫尔」——额头上贴着一张写着赫尔名字的纸条，怎么甩都甩不掉。

root: 拉丁语 adhaerere（黏着），由 ad-（向）与 haerere（黏附、停留）构成；本义是「贴住不放」，引申为遵守规则与追随他人。

sensesIntro.en: Sticking is the single image behind glue, rules and loyalty.
sensesIntro.cn: 「粘住」这一个意象，同时管着胶水、规则与忠诚。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a label that will not come off.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张揭不下来的标签。

branches.en: glue holding a label to glass
branches.cn: 胶水把标签固定在玻璃上

branches.en: wet paper clinging to a wall
branches.cn: 湿纸紧贴在墙上

branches.en: a worker keeping every safety rule
branches.cn: 工人条条遵守安全规定

branches.en: supporters staying with a leader
branches.cn: 拥护者不离开领袖

branches.en: staying fixed in conduct and in allegiance
branches.cn: 在行为与归属上都固定不动

intro.en: A prefix of direction on a root that means to stick.
intro.cn: 表示方向的词头，加在一个意为「粘住」的词根上。

latinIntro.en: The same root gives inhere and cohere.
latinIntro.cn: 同一词根还给出 inhere 与 cohere。

definition_zh: 产出、出产（粮食、收成）；屈服、让步；让路（交通）；名词：产量、收益
definition_en: to produce a crop or result, to give way, or the amount produced
core_image: 一棵压弯了枝的苹果树，果子垂到人手里
scene: 公路口立着一块牌子：前方施工，请让行。 These fields yield two crops a year.
sceneCN: 这里 yield 是「出产」（第 1 个义项：田里长出作物）；句意为这些田地一年出产两季作物。被果子压弯的树枝，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：出产、产生；屈服、让步；让路；弯曲、塌陷
名词：产量、收成；收益、利润率

collocations.phrase: give way / yield the right of way

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「柔软的；顺从的；出产的」
在 yielding 后加 -ly，义为「柔顺地」
加前缀 un- 构成，义为「不屈的、坚硬的」
近义词，义为「产量」，侧重产出量而非动作

senses.title: To produce from the land
senses.definition: to produce a crop, a natural product or a result
senses.definitionCN: 生产出作物、天然产物或结果
senses.example: The orchard yields a good crop of pears each autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 这片果园每年秋天都出产好收成。
senses.why: The oldest sense is of the earth giving its fruit; the ground hands over what it grew.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是土地献出果实：土地把长出来的东西交出来。

senses.title: To give way
senses.definition: to stop resisting and accept what is stronger
senses.definitionCN: 停止抵抗，接受更强的一方
senses.example: The government finally yielded to public pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 政府最终屈服于公众压力。
senses.why: From giving fruit, the word moved to giving ground: a defended position is handed over to the opponent.
senses.whyCN: 从献出果实到让出地面：防守的阵地被交给对手。

senses.title: To let others pass
senses.titleCN: 让行：交通中让别人先过
senses.definition: to allow other traffic to go first
senses.definitionCN: 在交通中让别人先行
senses.example: Cars must yield to pedestrians at this crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个路口，车辆必须给行人让行。
senses.why: This is the road version of giving way: one driver hands over the right to move first.
senses.whyCN: 这是「让」的道路版本：一位司机把先行的权利交出去。

senses.title: The amount produced
senses.definition: the quantity produced, as of crops or goods
senses.definitionCN: 出产的数量，如作物或产品
senses.example: Farmers worried about a lower rice yield this year.
senses.exampleCN: 农民担心今年水稻产量降低。
senses.why: The noun simply measures the verb: how much the land or the machine gave over.
senses.whyCN: 名词只是在度量动词：土地或机器交出了多少。

senses.title: The return on money
senses.definition: the profit or income produced by an investment
senses.definitionCN: 投资所产生的利润或收入
senses.example: The bond offers a yield of four percent.
senses.exampleCN: 这只债券提供百分之四的收益率。
senses.why: Money, like soil, can be made to yield; the return is the fruit of capital.
senses.whyCN: 钱也像土壤一样能出产；回报就是资本的果实。

senses.title: To bend or give under weight
senses.titleCN: 弯曲、塌陷：在重压下让开
senses.definition: to bend, break or give way under force
senses.definitionCN: 在受力时弯曲、断裂或塌陷
senses.example: The old chair yielded under his weight.
senses.exampleCN: 那把旧椅子在他的重量下塌了下去。
senses.why: Physical giving way: a solid thing stops resisting the load and moves aside.
senses.whyCN: 物理意义上的让：坚固之物不再抵抗重量，让开了。

intro.en: Yield descends from Old English gieldan, a Germanic word for paying what is due.
intro.cn: yield 源自古英语 gieldan，是日耳曼语中表示「付出应付之物」的词。

items.en: Gieldan meant to pay, to repay, or to give up what is owed.
items.cn: Gieldan 意为支付、偿还或交出应付之物。

items.en: The noun gield named a payment or a due amount.
items.cn: 名词 gield 指一笔付款或应付的数额。

items.en: The sense widened from paying money to giving up ground and producing crops.
items.cn: 词义从付钱扩大到让出地面和出产作物。

items.en: In agriculture and trade it settled as the regular word for output and return.
items.cn: 在农业与贸易中，它固定为表示产量与回报的常用词。

items.en: Traffic rules and finance both use it: yield the right of way, and yield on a bond.
items.cn: 交通规则与金融都用它：让行，以及债券的收益率。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers Germanic words with similar spelling and sound; the near-meaning group separates the several senses of giving.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写与读音相似的本土词；近义组按「让」的不同含义区分。

entries.definition: An area of open land; shares the -ield ending but not the root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「田地」，与 yield 只是尾音相近，词根不同。

entries.definition: A protective piece of armour or a guard.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「盾牌、保护」，形状相似。

entries.definition: An old verb meaning to castrate, from the same Germanic base as yield.
entries.definitionCN: 古动词，义为「阉割」，与 yield 同出日耳曼语词干。

entries.definition: An association of craftsmen; spelled alike but a different word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「行会」，拼写相近但词源不同。

entries.definition: To stop fighting and hand over control, more military than yield.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「投降、交出」，比 yield 更有军事色彩。

entries.definition: To accept authority or a decision, a more formal yielding.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「提交、屈从」，是更正式的让步。

entries.definition: To make or grow something, the plain verb behind sense one.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「生产、生长」，对应第 1 个义项。

entries.definition: The amount made; a neutral noun for yield in industry.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「产量」，工业语境里是中性的同义词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks link the farm picture to the road and the bank.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把田里的画面连到马路和银行。

normal.en: A field that gives fruit yields; the same word gives ground when you yield in traffic.
normal.cn: 出果子的田地叫 yield；在交通里让出地面也是 yield。

normal.en: To yield to pressure is to hand over your resistance like a crop handed over.
normal.cn: 屈服于压力，就像把作物交出去一样交出抵抗。

normal.en: Yield sign at a crossing: you give the right of way, not the argument.
normal.cn: 路口的让行标志：让的是先行权，不是道理。

normal.en: A bond's yield is the fruit of your money.
normal.cn: 债券的 yield 就是你的钱结的果。

normal.en: The old chair yielded: it gave up its shape under him.
normal.cn: 旧椅子 yielded：它在他身下放弃了原来的形状。

abstract.en: One idea under all senses: something holds, then lets go and hands over.
abstract.cn: 所有义项背后只有一个想法：先坚持，然后松手交出。

abstract.en: Earth gives fruit, people give ground, money gives return.
abstract.cn: 土地给果实，人让出地面，钱给出回报。

abstract.en: Picture the bend: a branch loaded with apples leans down to your hand.
abstract.cn: 想那个弯曲：挂满苹果的枝条弯到你的手边。

examples.en: The new farming method yielded twice as much wheat.
examples.cn: 新的耕作方法使小麦产量翻倍。

examples.en: She refused to yield on the question of safety.
examples.cn: 在安全问题上她拒不让步。

examples.en: Drivers must yield to cyclists at the roundabout.
examples.cn: 在环岛处司机必须给骑行者让行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一有得」——田里一有得，就是出产、有收成。

root: 古英语 gieldan（支付、交出）

sensesIntro.en: One Germanic verb of handing over runs through farm, road and bank.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个表示「交出」的日耳曼动词，贯穿田间、马路与银行。

core.en: to give over what one has
core.cn: 把自己有的东西交出去

branches.en: HARVEST LINE: the land gives its crop and the amount is counted.
branches.cn: 收成线：土地交出作物，数量被计量。

branches.en: PRESSURE LINE: resistance stops and control is handed over.
branches.cn: 压力线：抵抗停止，主动权交出。

branches.en: ROAD LINE: one driver lets another go first.
branches.cn: 道路线：一位司机让别人先行。

branches.en: MONEY LINE: capital produces a return.
branches.cn: 资金线：资本产生回报。

branches.en: WEIGHT LINE: a solid thing bends under a load.
branches.cn: 重量线：坚固之物在重压下弯曲。

intro.en: yield is a native Germanic word, so its parts are listed as English building blocks rather than Latin affixes.
intro.cn: yield 是日耳曼语本土词，这里把各部件当作英语构词块列出。

latinIntro.en: No Latin affixes are involved here, so nothing is listed as Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这里不涉及拉丁词缀，故不列拉丁条目。

items.example: Yielding describes what gives way easily.
items.exampleCN: yielding 形容容易让开的东西。

items.example: It looks like yield but means a guard.
items.exampleCN: 它形似 yield，但意思是盾。

definition_zh: 克制；限制；约束措施
definition_en: the quality of controlling your behavior, or something that limits action
core_image: 一双手按住桌沿，强忍着不让自己拍桌而起
scene: 面对无礼的质问，她以极大的克制保持平静，没有提高嗓门。 Faced with a rude question, she showed great restraint and stayed calm without raising her voice.
sceneCN: 这里 restraint 是「克制」（第 1 个义项：控制自己的情绪与行为）；句意：面对无礼的质问，她以极大的克制保持平静，没有提高嗓门。

derivatives.zh: 抑制；阻止
克制的
无节制的

senses.title: Self-control
senses.definition: the ability to control your feelings or behavior
senses.definitionCN: 控制自己情绪或行为的能力
senses.example: He answered the insult with remarkable restraint.
senses.exampleCN: 面对辱骂，他以惊人的克制回应。
senses.why: The noun names the act of the verb restrain, so it is the holding back itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指动词 restrain 的行为，也就是「拉住」本身。

senses.title: A limit on action
senses.definition: a rule or condition that limits what people can do
senses.definitionCN: 限制人们行动范围的规则或条件
senses.example: The new law places restraints on advertising.
senses.exampleCN: 新法律对广告作出了限制。
senses.why: Something that holds people back is a restraint on their action.
senses.whyCN: 拉住人们的东西，就是对行动的限制。

senses.title: A physical device
senses.definition: a seat belt or other device that holds a person safely
senses.definitionCN: 安全带或其他把人固定住的装置
senses.example: The child seat has strong restraints for the shoulders.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童座椅有结实的肩部约束带。
senses.why: A belt physically restrains the body, so it is called a restraint.
senses.whyCN: 安全带在身体上拉住人，所以被称为 restraint。

intro.en: Restraint is the noun of restrain, from Latin restringere, to draw tight.
intro.cn: restraint 是 restrain 的名词形式，源自拉丁语 restringere（拉紧）。

items.en: Restringere means to hold back or bind.
items.cn: restringere 意为拉住或捆绑。

items.en: Restreindre means to check or limit.
items.cn: restreindre 意为抑制或限制。

items.en: Restraint names the act of holding back.
items.cn: restraint 指拉住的行为。

items.en: It also names rules and safety devices.
items.cn: 它也指规则与安全装置。

items.en: Wage restraint limits pay increases.
items.cn: wage restraint 限制工资上涨。

note.en: Restraint is the noun beside restrain, close to control and limit.
note.cn: restraint 是与 restrain 对应的名词，与控制和限制相近。

entries.definition: to hold back
calm and controlled
without limits
the ability to control yourself
a rule that limits something
keeping within reasonable limits

normalIntro.en: Restraint is what a taut rope does: it keeps force in check.
normalIntro.cn: restraint 就像绷紧的绳子：它把力量控制在范围之内。

normal.en: Show restraint means do not act on every impulse.
normal.cn: show restraint 意为不要一有冲动就行动。

normal.en: Without restraint means with no control at all.
normal.cn: without restraint 意为完全不加控制。

normal.en: A restraint on trade is a limit on business.
normal.cn: a restraint on trade 是对商业的限制。

normal.en: A seat belt is a physical restraint.
normal.cn: 安全带是一种身体约束装置。

normal.en: Compare restriction: a restraint holds back, a restriction sets rules.
normal.cn: 对比 restriction：restraint 拉住行为，restriction 制定规则。

abstract.en: Picture a hand held flat on a table to stop a fist.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手平按在桌上，压住想挥出的拳头。

abstract.en: Imagine a river held by a quiet dam.
abstract.cn: 想象一条被安静水坝拦住的河。

abstract.en: Think of a voice kept low on purpose.
abstract.cn: 想象一个故意压低的声音。

examples.en: She spoke with restraint about the painful subject.
examples.cn: 谈到这个痛苦的话题时，她说话很有克制。

examples.en: The government imposed restraints on imports.
examples.cn: 政府对进口施加了限制。

examples.en: Make sure the child seat restraints are fastened.
examples.cn: 确保儿童座椅的约束带已系好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「restrain（拉住）＋ t」——拉住的那股劲，就是克制与限制；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 restringere（拉紧）→ 古法语 restreindre → restrain ＋名词词尾 → restraint，核心义「拉住、限制的力量或状态」。

sensesIntro.en: Restraint begins as inner self-control, widens to a rule that limits action, and ends as a physical safety device.
sensesIntro.cn: restraint 从内在的自我克制，扩展到限制行动的规则，最后指身体上的安全装置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressed on a table to hold a fist back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按在桌上，压住想挥出的拳头。

branches.en: The first sense is control from inside.
branches.cn: 首要义项是来自内部的自我控制。

branches.en: Rules from outside also restrain action.
branches.cn: 外部规则同样限制行动。

branches.en: A belt physically holds the body in place.
branches.cn: 安全装置在身体上把人固定住。

branches.en: A calm person and a firm rule both prevent excess.
branches.cn: 冷静的人与严格的规则都能防止过度。

branches.en: Safety devices replace self-control in a crash.
branches.cn: 发生碰撞时，安全装置接替自我控制发挥作用。

intro.en: Restraint adds a noun ending to restrain, whose root means to draw tight.
intro.cn: restraint 在 restrain 上加名词词尾，其词根意为拉紧。

latinIntro.en: Latin stringere, to draw tight, underlies the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stringere（拉紧）是整个词族的根基。
